原力引擎（上海）智能科技有限公司（以下简称“原力引擎”）是一家AI for Engineering（AI4Engineering）企业。投资界（ID：pedaily2012）8月26日消息，原力引擎宣布完成天使+轮近5000万元融资。本轮融资由上海国投旗下上海未来产业基金和上海科创集团共同领投，复旦科创加注领投，龙芯创投、成为资本等跟投，光源资本担任独 家财务顾问。本轮资金将主要用于生成式仿真与智能控制引擎的持续研发、聚变等标杆场景的装置级验证、能源与高端制造等行业客户拓展，并持续强化全球顶 尖复合型人才团队建设。
原力引擎由吴泰霖教授创立，其本科毕业于北京大学物理学院，获麻省理工学院物理学博士学位，后于斯坦福大学计算机系Jure Leskovec教授课题组从事博士后研究；现任西湖大学工学院特聘研究员、助理教授，西湖大学人工智能与科学仿真发现实验室负责人。他长期研究大规模科学仿真、物理系统控制与科学发现，曾与博士生导师Max Tegmark教授提出“理论学习”的新学习范式和以AI物理学家（AI Physicist）为核心的系列方法，并在生成式AI赋能复杂物理系统仿真、控制、设计方面做出一系列领域开创性工作。
公司以可控核聚变为首 个高难度验证场景，并将相关能力拓展至油气、核电、3C及航空航天等能源与高端制造领域。在上述场景中，模型不仅要“算得快”，还必须满足高精度、泛化性、实时性、安全边界和现场部署等工程约束。
传统数值求解器和CAE软件是工程研发的重要基础，但面对多物理场、多尺度、多部件耦合系统，通常需要针对具体几何、边界条件与物理过程构建求解流程，当其进入参数扫描、反演设计和控制策略训练的内循环时，计算与工程成本会被进一步放大。
原力引擎并非简单替代传统求解器，而是以数值求解与实验数据为高可信训练基础，通过神经算子、扩散模型等方法学习物理场演化及条件分布，在推理阶段完成快速预测与耦合生成。公司已在流体、油藏和等离子体等复杂物理仿真任务上实现数十倍至数百倍加速，部分任务可由传统的小时或天级计算压缩至秒级，并且可通过真实装置与工业现场验证持续校准模型。
原力引擎在聚变领域正与国内聚变科研机构及头部商业聚变企业推进等离子体仿真、软着陆控制和位形控制合作，公司研发的生成式AI控制算法已完成装置上机实验验证并实现优越控制性能。公司希望以聚变场景对模型精度、实时性和安全性的严苛要求，反向锤炼可复用的物理建模与控制能力。

日前，中国光互连初创企业上海芯光界智能科技有限公司（下称“芯光界”）宣布，公司日前已顺利完成天使轮融资。本轮由创投行业头部机构启明创投独家投资，融资总额达亿元人民币。融资资金将为公司核心技术研发、产品迭代及团队建设提供坚实资金保障。后续公司将集中核心资源攻坚行业关键核心技术，加速NPO产品商业化落地、CPO前沿技术预研与技术迭代，推进产品客户验证与场景适配，同步吸纳领域高端人才，夯实公司的核心优势和技术壁垒。
芯光界于2026年5月启动，并迅速完成种子轮数千万元融资。公司由国际知名硅光及光互连方向顶尖专家创立。芯光界聚焦前沿光互连和硅光通信技术的创新研发与成果转化，致力于为全球AI智算集群提供核心光互连产品和下一代全栈光互连解决方案，旨在成为全球AI智算集群光互连技术的定义者。公司遵循“NPO切入、CPO主流、OIO布局”的三阶段技术路径，构建了从芯片设计、封装耦合到系统级信号完整性的全链路自研能力。核心研发团队覆盖硅光芯片设计、先进封装、高频信号完整性等领域，各板块负责人均拥有15年以上行业从业经验，具备国内头部企业工作经历与成熟项目交付经验。芯光界首款NPO光引擎已与国内头部GPU厂商及数据中心客户启动技术方案对接与验证，并积极参与ODCC、CPX MSA等核心行业标准制定。
芯光界创始人兼CEO董坡表示：“AI算力产业高速发展，带动光互连技术需求持续升级，高集成、高性能的光互连方案已成为算力集群迭代的重要支撑。本次获得亿元天使轮融资是对团队技术积累与赛道发展前景的充分认可。未来我们将持续深耕光互连核心技术，加速产品迭代与商业化落地，打磨更具竞争力的行业解决方案，助力算力光互连产业创新发展。”
启明创投主管合伙人周志峰表示：“随着大规模AI算力集群加速落地，高集成、高性能的高速光互连技术已成为算力产业升级的核心刚需，赛道增量空间广阔。芯光界团队具备扎实的底层技术功底与成熟的工程化、商业化落地能力，在技术自研、产品量产与客户落地方面优势显著。我们十分看好公司在AI算力光互连赛道的发展潜力，期待公司持续深耕技术、打磨标杆产品，持续赋能算力光互连产业创新发展。”

U.K.-based manufacturing software startup CloudNC announced a $20 million Series B extension round on Wednesday, bringing its lifetime total amount raised to $128 million. The company’s last major raise was four years ago, its co-founder and CEO Theo Saville told TechCrunch.
Saville launched CloudNC in 2015 with Chris Emery, now the company’s chief science officer, and offers AI-powered CAM Assist software that automates parts of computer numerical control (CNC) machining. CNC is the process of using computer-controlled machines to cut or shape materials precisely into the parts that are then used in automotive, defense, or consumer hardware industries.
Before a part can be cut, Saville said, a machinist or a computer-aided manufacturing programmer has to decide issues like how a part should be held or what tools should be used, Saville said.

The financing comprises $223 million in Series B equity and a $445-million credit facility led by CTBC. The Series B was led by San Francisco-based AI and robotics investor ARCHIV, with participation from NVIDIA.
Asia-Pacific investors, including DSC Investment, Trend Micro, KB Investment, Kyobo Life and KT Corporation, also participated in the funding round.
GMI Cloud said the funding will support capacity expansion in the US, Taiwan, and other APAC markets, building on its Taiwan AI Factory launched in 2025 and a Japan sovereign AI initiative announced earlier this year.
The company will also use the proceeds to expand its inference services and hire additional staff, per the announcement. It counts Fireworks, Higgsfield, Nous Research, OpenRouter and Trend Micro among its customers.

NanoCo, the company behind security-focused OpenClaw alternative NanoClaw, has raised an oversubscribed $12 million seed round following a viral launch, its founders tell TechCrunch.
The funding was led by Valley Capital Partners and saw participation from Docker, Vercel, Monday.com, Slow Ventures, and angels like Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face.
In a matter of weeks, NanoClaw creator Gavriel Cohen (pictured above, left) said he went from coding the project on his couch to receiving viral endorsements from Andrej Karpathy and Singapore’s foreign minister, fielding inbound interest from dozens of investors, and even a roughly $20 million acquisition offer that he and his brother and co-founder, Lazer Cohen (pictured above, right), declined.
“It was under six weeks from committing the first lines of code to a term sheet,” Gavriel told TechCrunch.
“There was a lot of inbound and interest,” he added. “People reaching out in DMs on X and sending emails.” He estimated that about 50 or more founders and tech executives sent DMs asking to invest.
One of them was Delangue, who dropped a note: “I like what you’re doing with NanoClaw.” Gavriel then responded in kind, telling the Hugging Face CEO that he liked the company’s tiny robot, Reachy Mini, and hoped to run NanoClaw on it one day.
The two programmers then started talking shop, and Gavriel eventually asked Delangue if he was interested in angel investing and secured a yes.
As it turns out, an active member of NanoClaw’s open source community is already working on running it on Reachy Mini, Gavriel says.
As we previously reported, interest in NanoClaw skyrocketed after AI researcher Andrej Karpathy tweeted his praise for it. But the project really began to snowball after the foreign minister of Singapore called NanoClaw his “second brain” in a Facebook post that went viral.
NanoClaw was created as a secure alternative to OpenClaw to assist the Cohen brothers with their previous startup, an AI marketing firm that used agents to do much of the work. But instead of running directly on a computer, with access to all services and credentials, NanoClaw runs sandboxed in a container — a practice that is becoming a common solution to running more secure, OpenClaw-like setups.

2026 年 1 月 5 日 —— 全球领先消费级 AR 品牌雷鸟创新（RayNeo）宣布近期完成新一轮超 10 亿元融资。本轮融资由中国移动链长基金与中信金石（旗下茅台金石、金石成长等基金）领投，中国联通旗下联创创新基金等机构共同参与。
此次融资标志着国内运营商首次战略投资智能眼镜赛道，意味着 AR 终端正式进入国家通信基础设施的战略视野。持续的资金注入，将为雷鸟创新的技术研发与全球市场拓展提供强劲动能，并推动公司加速跻身独角兽企业行列。

十年轮回：运营商押注下一代“ iPhone ”
十余年前，中国运营商作为关键推手，以基础网络建设、“充话费送手机”、生态共建等模式深度参与智能手机的爆发式普及，彻底改变了中国消费者的数字生活方式。如今，相似的场景正在 AR 领域重演。
面对“空间计算时代”这一战略窗口，中国两大通信巨头联手注资雷鸟创新，背后是清晰的产业判断：在运营商的战略图谱中，AR 智能眼镜已不再是“极客玩具”，而是智能手机之后的下一代主流个人终端的既定答案。
运营商入局带来的不仅是资本背书，也标志着双方正式建立起深度战略合作关系，后续将围绕市场渠道共建、商业模式创新与核心技术生态展开全方位协同：借助运营商覆盖全国的线下服务网点、数以亿计的用户基数，雷鸟 AR 智能眼镜将触达更广泛的消费群体；“充话费送眼镜”“合约机”等运营商擅长的服务模式，将大幅降低用户对 AR 智能眼镜的尝试门槛，成为后续市场爆发的关键推手。同时，运营商在 eSIM、5G 等关键通讯技术，AI 服务及内容生态等方面的资源，也将为雷鸟创新的产品演进提供强大支撑。
即将在 CES 2026 亮相的雷鸟 X3 Pro Project eSIM，正是双方协同的重要成果。该产品集成了 eSIM 通信模块与 4G 协议支持，无需手机联网，即可实现包括拨打和接听电话、多模态 AI 对话、高质量 AI 实时翻译、在线流媒体音乐等多项功能，成为首款真正具备独立通信能力的消费级 AR 智能眼镜。
过往，智能眼镜始终被诟病为“手机的附属品”—— 没有手机，眼镜便失去了大部分功能。而 eSIM 的加入将使眼镜进化为“完全体”：结合雷鸟在 AI 大模型、空间计算以及 AR 应用生态上的深厚积累，AR 智能眼镜将真正进化为一个全场景的个人计算中心，独立承载通信、计算、显示、交互的完整能力。

智能眼镜正在被推向消费电子领域最受关注的位置。IDC数据显示，2025年全球AI智能眼镜出货量同比增幅超过200%；中国市场增速更为显著，洛图科技统计显示，2026上半年国内智能眼镜全渠道销量已达90.9万台，同比增长85.5%，对应销售额18.8亿元，同比增长98.7%。
市场规模快速抬升，但能够真正撬动大众用户心智的标杆级产品仍未出现。过去几年，行业主流产品形态始终停留在“让眼镜能显示”的初级阶段，普遍采用Birdbath方案加外接计算单元的组合，本质上是把“显示”做到了眼镜上，但“算力”仍依赖外部设备。
影目科技创始人兼CEO杨龙昇指出，“显示本身并不构成独立的终端价值。用户真正需要的不是一个戴在脸上的屏幕，而是一个能脱离手机独立运作的智能体。市场需求正在经历从‘手机配件’向‘独立终端’的关键转折。”
这一判断的背后，是产品结构的切实变化。2026年一季度，带屏AI智能眼镜销量占比已升至60%；一体式AR眼镜与分体式产品的销量占比，更从2025年一季度的9:91快速转变为2026年二季度的47:53。可以看到，用户对“独立终端”的接受度正处于迅猛提升态势。
在杨龙昇看来，智能眼镜是否成为“下一代终端”，必须回答三个问题——它能不能脱离手机独立运行？它能不能提供手机给不了的价值？它能不能在日常佩戴中做到无感？
它们的答案都指向同一个方向：一体化。
影目科技成立于2020年底，作为国内最早入局消费级智能眼镜的品牌之一，团队一开始便坚定轻量一体化的技术路线，把光学显示、本地计算、AI感知算力收拢集成在眼镜机身之内，以摆脱对手机、外接主机等外部设备的依赖。

specificationFacts.source_quote: Korea Telecom launched the KT NPU LLM Station on Wednesday — the first commercially available enterprise AI appliance to pair a Korean-made inference chip with a Korean-developed large language model in a single on-premises server — targeting a regulated-industry market that has been structurally locked out of generative AI by the country's strict network-separation rules .

The important caveat for enterprise buyers is scale. At 32 billion parameters, Mi:dm K 2.5 Pro sits well below the frontier-model tier — the leading models from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic operate at hundreds of billions to trillions of effective parameters. Korean sovereign AI competitors SK Telecom and LG AI Research released models in the 700-billion-parameter range in late July 2026 — covered in detail in our prior sovereign AI coverage . Mi:dm K 2.5 Pro is not designed to compete on raw capability with frontier models; it is designed to deliver enterprise-grade Korean-language reasoning within the memory and power budget of an on-premises server that complies with mangjuri. That is a genuine tradeoff, and buyers in regulated sectors should weigh it: a 32B-parameter model running locally is materially less capable than a 400B-parameter model accessed via API — but for an organization whose data cannot legally leave its facility, the API option does not exist.

supplyFacts.source_quote: L&T Deploys India’s First 10,000-GPU Unified AI Cluster for Together AI in Chennai

India AI data center deployment reaches a new frontier: L&T has secured a $1.05 to $1.57 billion contract to deploy 10,000 NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in a single NVLink-connected cluster at its...

India's largest engineering conglomerate, Larsen & Toubro, announced today that it has secured a contract worth ₹10,000 crore to ₹15,000 crore (approximately $1.05 billion to $1.57 billion USD) to deploy 10,000 NVIDIA B300 "Blackwell Ultra" GPUs in a single interconnected cluster at Vyoma.AI's Chennai data center campus. The customer is Together AI, the San Francisco-based open-source AI cloud provider that crossed $1.15 billion in bookings earlier this year. What makes this deal different from every prior India AI data center announcement is not the dollar figure — it is the word "single-cluster."A distributed deployment of 10,000 GPUs spread across independently networked servers and a unified single-cluster of 10,000 GPUs connected by a shared NVLink fabric are not the same machine. They are not even close to the same machine. The distinction is the entire editorial point of this article.What "Single-Cluster" Actually Means: Architecture, Bandwidth, and What It UnlocksWhen NVIDIA ships the B300 in its DGX B300 server configuration, it packs eight B300 SXM GPUs onto a single baseboard. Those eight GPUs connect to each other through NVLink 5, NVIDIA's proprietary fifth-generation interconnect, which delivers 1.8 terabytes per second of bidirectional bandwidth per GPU. A NVSwitch chip inside the chassis provides full all-to-all connectivity — any GPU can communicate with any other GPU at the full NVLink bandwidth without going through a slower external network. The complete NVIDIA DGX B300 specifications confirm a total system bandwidth of 14.4 terabytes per second across the eight-GPU node.Now multiply that by 1,250 servers — the approximate number of DGX B300 nodes required to reach 10,000 GPUs — and connect them using high-speed inter-node networking. The result is a compute fabric in which all 10,000 GPUs are addressable as a single unified system: jobs can be scheduled across the entire cluster as if it were one giant accelerator, because the NVLink interconnect architecture was designed explicitly to allow that. This is what "single-cluster" means, and it is what a disaggregated arrangement of the same GPUs — spread across separate deployments, different buildings, or independent cloud regions — cannot replicate.The engineering reason this matters is gradient synchronization. Training a large AI model requires all GPUs to periodically share updated weight gradients through an operation called all-reduce. In a small cluster, this operation is fast. In a large cluster, it becomes the dominant bottleneck — if the interconnect fabric cannot move gradient data across all nodes quickly enough, GPUs spend more time waiting than computing, and the scaling efficiency of additional hardware collapses. The 14.4 terabytes per second NVLink bandwidth within a DGX node is orders of magnitude faster than even InfiniBand networking between separate servers. The single-cluster designation is NVIDIA's claim that the architecture allows this scaling to work across the full fleet rather than degrading at node boundaries.The practical consequence: a 10,000-GPU single NVLink cluster can run multi-node fine-tuning jobs and large-scale training runs that are simply not feasible on the same number of GPUs in a disaggregated arrangement. Prior India data center announcements — including Meta's 168-megawatt campus at Jamnagar, Gujarat — described power capacity and general-purpose compute infrastructure. This one describes a specific interconnect architecture and the class of workloads it enables.The B300 Itself: Memory, Bandwidth, and Why the Upgrade From H100 Is Non-LinearThe NVIDIA B300 — formally the Blackwell Ultra GPU — is NVIDIA's current volume-production flagship for data center AI inference and training. A single B300 GPU carries 288 gigabytes of HBM3e memory at 8 terabytes per second of memory bandwidth. An eight-GPU DGX B300 node accordingly holds 2.3 terabytes of total fast GPU memory, enough to run a 405-billion parameter model — such as Meta's Llama 3.1 405B — in full 16-bit precision on a single server without splitting the model across nodes. That memory ceiling matters for the agentic and multi-step reasoning workloads Together AI's platform increasingly serves.The performance gap over the previous generation is non-linear. Independent benchmarks from SemiAnalysis InferenceX — an open-source reproducible benchmark suite running verified results nightly on actual production hardware — show the B300 delivering more than 4,000 tokens per second per GPU on DeepSeek R1 at a 38 tokens-per-second-per-user latency target, compared to 276 tokens per second per GPU on the H100 — a roughly 14-fold throughput improvement for that workload. The B300 vs H100 benchmark data also shows cost advantage is larger still: B300 produces tokens at approximately $0.16 per million versus $1.32 per million for the H100 at the same latency, a more than 700 percent cost improvement.At the rack scale, NVIDIA's GB300 NVL72 systems — 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs in a single liquid-cooled rack — deliver up to 50 times higher throughput per megawatt and 35 times lower cost per token compared to NVIDIA's prior Hopper H100 platform for agentic workloads, according to SemiAnalysis InferenceX data cited by NVIDIA. These figures are for the rack-scale NVL72 configuration; individual DGX B300 server performance scales accordingly.Each B300 GPU operates at a thermal design power of 1,400 watts — nearly double the H100's 700 watts. At 10,000 GPUs, that totals up to 14 megawatts of GPU power alone, before server overhead, networking, and cooling loads are counted. Running this cluster requires purpose-built liquid cooling infrastructure; standard air-cooled data centers cannot manage B300 density at this scale. Vyoma's Chennai campus is designed for 250 megawatts in Phase 1 with 150 MVA of power infrastructure already in place — the physical plant was engineered for exactly this class of hardware.Together AI: Why a US AI Company Chose India for a Frontier ClusterTogether AI is not a general cloud provider. Founded in 2022 in San Francisco, the company runs an inference and training platform for open-weight AI models — DeepSeek, MiniMax, Kimi, GLM, and dozens of others — through an API compatible with OpenAI's interface. The platform processes 400 trillion tokens monthly for developers and enterprise customers. Together AI does not build its own foundation models; its value is the infrastructure that makes other organizations' open-source models cheaper and faster to run than proprietary alternatives.The Chennai cluster is part of a rapid global expansion. Just two days before the L&T announcement, Together AI and IBM disclosed a $240 million multi-year agreement under which IBM Cloud will deploy a large cluster of NVIDIA HGX B300 systems to serve Together AI's inference platform, with availability expected in the first quarter of 2027. Together AI closed an $800 million Series C on July 1, 2026, at an $8.3 billion valuation, with Aramco Ventures as lead investor and NVIDIA among the participants. Together AI CEO Vipul Ved Prakash has described the company's infrastructure buildout as "the biggest infrastructure build-out in human history."The India decision reflects three converging factors that make Chennai specifically attractive for the platform's expansion. First, India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act of 2023, whose implementing rules were finalized in November 2025, creates meaningful compliance incentives for enterprises that can process Indian user data within the country. Indian enterprise customers using Together AI's inference from a Chennai cluster operate under a materially simpler regulatory posture than those routing workloads to US-based data centers. Second, the cost of power, land, and infrastructure in India remains significantly lower than in the United States or Europe, where data center power costs have surged alongside the GPU buildout. Third, India's developer community — the second-largest contributor to GitHub AI projects globally, according to GitHub's annual developer data — represents a large and growing demand base for the inference services Together AI offers.L&T's Corporate Architecture for the AI EraThe deal is executed through a newly built corporate structure. In June 2026, Vyoma.AI — L&T's data center and cloud services subsidiary — incorporated a wholly owned entity called LTN Compute Private Limited to build out AI compute infrastructure and provide technology-enabled services. LTN Compute is the operating vehicle through which L&T is formally entering what the company calls the "AI Factory" business: not just constructing the buildings that house data centers, but owning, operating, and monetizing the GPU infrastructure inside them.L&T separately agreed earlier this week to transfer its data center business to Vyoma.AI for ₹1,400 crore (approximately $147 million USD), consolidating the infrastructure business under Vyoma as its dedicated vehicle. L&T Chairman and Managing Director S N Subrahmanyan framed the Chennai deal in terms of the company's broader infrastructure ambitions: "Artificial intelligence is becoming foundational to every industry and AI factories will power this transformation. Our deployment of an Nvidia B300 AI factory for Together AI marks a significant milestone in L&T's gigawatt AI infrastructure mission."L&T has separately established a broader partnership with NVIDIA to develop gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure across India, including plans to scale GPU clusters at the Chennai campus to 30 megawatts and build a new 40-megawatt facility in Mumbai. The Together AI contract is the first large, signed deployment that turns those plans into hardware.India's AI Compute Race: Where the Chennai Deal FitsIndia's national AI compute program, the IndiaAI Mission, was approved by Cabinet in March 2024 with a funding outlay of ₹10,371 crore (approximately $1.09 billion USD) over five years. As of mid-2026, the program has deployed approximately 34,000 GPUs, accessible to startups, academic researchers, and government agencies at subsidized rates of around ₹65 per GPU-hour (approximately $0.68 USD per GPU-hour). Officials have set a target of 100,000 public GPUs by December 2026, with national GPU capacity — including private deployments — expected to exceed 200,000 by year-end.The L&T-Together AI deal, at 10,000 B300 GPUs, represents roughly 29 percent of the IndiaAI Mission's entire public target in a single private deployment. More significantly, B300 GPUs are not equivalent to H100s on a one-to-one basis: the per-GPU performance advantage means 10,000 B300s perform a substantially larger volume of inference work than 10,000 H100s would. The effective compute contribution of this single cluster to India's national AI capacity is materially larger than the raw GPU count suggests.Chennai's emergence as a focal point for this investment is deliberate. The city ranks second among Indian data center markets, contributing approximately 21 percent of the country's total data center capacity, according to Blackridge Research. Equinix opened its Chennai data center in September 2025, specifically citing the city's position near anticipated submarine cable landing sites. The L&T campus at Vyoma operates in the same geography, with a gigawatt-scale site whose Phase 1 capacity is 250 megawatts.Global hyperscalers have made separate India commitments: Microsoft and Amazon targeting $52.5 billion in Indian AI and digital infrastructure; Google announcing a $15 billion AI data hub investment; and OpenAI partnering with Tata Group for one gigawatt of capacity. What the L&T-Together AI deal adds to that picture is different in kind: a US AI cloud provider that specifically serves open-weight model inference — not proprietary models, not a general cloud — deploying its most compute-intensive cluster outside the United States in South Asia, under an Indian operating entity. The full landscape of those India hyperscaler commitments provides context for the scale of current investment.The Geography of AI Compute Is ShiftingThe deeper implication of this deal is geographic. Since frontier AI infrastructure emerged as a strategically meaningful asset class, it has been concentrated almost exclusively in the United States, Europe, and parts of East Asia. Data centers in those regions hold the vast majority of the world's most advanced AI compute — the GPU clusters capable of training and serving the models that define the current frontier of AI capability.The Together AI-L&T contract represents a structural departure from that pattern. A US AI cloud provider of significant scale — one that crossed $1.15 billion in annual bookings and serves 400 trillion monthly tokens — has chosen to anchor a portion of its global compute infrastructure in India, under an Indian operator, running the most advanced hardware NVIDIA currently ships in volume. That is not a speculative AI-infrastructure announcement. LTN Compute had not commenced business operations as recently as June 2026. It is now the operating entity behind India's largest single-cluster AI deployment.For Indian enterprise customers evaluating whether to route AI workloads to US-based inference endpoints or a domestic provider, the answer is now materially different than it was last month. The latency advantage of a Chennai cluster over a US-based endpoint — measured in tens of milliseconds for real-time inference — is substantial for the interactive and agentic applications Together AI's platform increasingly supports. Together AI has not disclosed a pricing schedule or customer-facing launch date for the Chennai cluster, but the infrastructure is being built now.Currency conversions in this article are approximate, calculated at the USD/INR exchange rate as of August 13, 2026 (approximately ₹95.43 per USD), and are subject to change.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhat is the difference between a single-cluster GPU deployment and a distributed GPU deployment?

In a single-cluster deployment, all GPUs are addressable as a unified compute fabric through a shared high-bandwidth interconnect — in this case, NVIDIA's NVLink architecture. Any GPU in the cluster can communicate directly with any other GPU at full interconnect bandwidth, without routing through slower external networks. In a disaggregated or distributed deployment, GPUs are spread across separate servers or locations connected by standard Ethernet or InfiniBand, which offers much lower bandwidth for the all-reduce gradient-synchronization operations that large AI training runs require. A single-cluster architecture enables training jobs that scale efficiently to tens of thousands of GPUs; a distributed arrangement of the same hardware would degrade in scaling efficiency because the inter-node communication becomes the bottleneck.Why did Together AI choose India for a frontier GPU cluster, and what does this mean for enterprises routing AI workloads from South Asia?

community.content: 🌕月满中秋，一路有你 又是一年中秋，月亮慢慢圆了，归家的脚步也近了。 中秋总有一种温柔的力量，让忙碌的人停一停，让相隔很远的人重新想起彼此，也让我们在向前赶路时，记得回头看看一路陪伴自己的人。 🥮不知不觉，破局已经走过三年半。 三年半里，AI在快速变化，新的工具与机会不断出现，而我们也从最初的摸索走到了今天。 有人在这里学会了新的技能，有人完成了第一个作品，有人收获了第一笔副业收入，也有人在迷茫和受挫时，因为圈友的一句鼓励重新出发。 我们常说破局，但真正的破局，或许不只是抓住一次机会、获得一份收入， 更是在面对不确定时依然愿意尝试，在独自摸索的路上，遇见一群愿意分享经验、彼此搭把手的同行者。 🤝感谢每一位圈友的信任与陪伴。 是你们让破局不只是一个学习AI、探索副业的社区，更成为一个有温度、有连接的地方。…

community.author: findyi
community.content: 我在这里郑重说一下： 每一个社群都有自己的发展策略，大家做的选择都不一样，我表示尊重。 但对于破局来说：除非破局哪一天做不下去了、破产了，否则绝无可能。 如果破局能做大做强，甚至上市，我直接给AI之心持有圈友换成破局股份。 AI之心是破局圈友们历史给破局做过贡献后，破局对大家的感恩和回馈。 破局精神内核最重要的是感恩文化，而不是追求我们自己赚多少钱。 破局有这么多优秀的星火师、教练、星推官、组局官、领队、志愿者，是那些持续给破局做贡献的圈友们才让破局无比强大。 破局的感恩回馈理应是持续的！ 我们同时也希望这套文化内核能让大家也能相互之间感恩，比如感恩教会你的教练、感恩帮大家组局的组局官、感恩给大家写文章的星火师和内容创作者、感恩督促你的领队志愿者、感恩给大家做服务破局员工。 另外我们也会不断增加AI之心体系能…

viewpoints.originalContent: Reject non-understanding. Slop grenades are not just code and PRs. We run a real risk that *reading* gets entirely discounted, because of the exhaustion of getting low-quality and unverified AI prose being thrown at you all the time. There's a thread going viral about a 'perf improvement' attributed to a compiler change. The PR *description* itself has the AI telling this person it's *not* due to the compiler change, it's how the algorithms and data structures have changed. And the implication is that a similar win could have been attained otherwise. I want AI in the service of understanding the universe and enhancing human cognition and creativity.

viewpoints.translatedContent: AI领域真是疯狂的一天。前沿模型刚刚大幅降价，Opus 5.5价格下调，现在GPT-6 Sol和Luna又把token价格降低了50%。AI中每个任务成本（在同类对比基础上）下降的速度，是历史上任何其他技术都无法比拟的。而每当AI成本下降，你可以部署智能体来应对的用例就会急剧增加。这就是杰文斯悖论在智能体上的应用。这些改进将直接推动AI在经济中更广泛地扩散，因为我们可以用智能体来处理我们所有的数据、扫描代码中的安全问题、通读所有日志数据来做决策、在工作流中部署智能体集群，等等。token成本与这些用例能否大规模开放直接相关。
viewpoints.originalContent: What an insane day in AI. The frontier models just became substantially cheaper, with the Opus 5.5 price cuts, and now with GPT-6 Sol and Luna dropping token prices by 50%. The rate at which the cost per task (on a like-for-like basis) drops in AI is unlike any other type of technology in history. And every time the cost of AI drops, the use-cases you can deploy agents against dramatically increase. This is Jevons paradox applied to agents. These improvements will directly lead to broader diffusion of AI in the economy as we can use agents to process all of our data, scan our code for security issues, read through all log data to make decisions, have agent swarms in workflows, and much more. The cost of tokens is directly correlated to these use-cases being opened up at scale.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 在Box，我们一直在使用Box Agent测试Opus 5.5处理各种涉及非结构化数据的复杂企业知识工作任务。总体而言，我们看到了前沿能力水平，与Opus 5相比性能有了重大提升。与Opus 5相比，使用的token减少了63%，冗长度降低了42%，速度提升了30%。而且模型本身也更便宜，因此对于企业将要进行的任何智能体计算机使用、编码、分析或数据工作来说，这都是一个重大胜利。以下是我们执行的各种行业测试中任务成功和性能提升的一些示例：• 金融服务——尽职调查（任务准确率+39%）：一年的交易记录，任务是找出收购目标定价工具中的每一处计算错误。Opus 5.5在每次尝试中都取得了满分结果，所用字数仅为Opus 5的一半，总体消耗的token减少了82%。• 技术——云成本分析（任务准确率+65%）：确定一家公司实际应当对其云支出做出哪些改变。Opus 5.5为留存计算选择了正确的基础，并全程保持了源数据单位约定的一致性，因此最终得出的数字确实站得住脚。它所用时间仅为Opus 5的一半，token减少了70%。• 消费品——客户账户分析（任务准确率+17%）：为某个客户账户设定引导目标，需要综合已签署合同、满意度追踪表和团队指标表。合同从未说明高级/初级人员比例，因此Opus 5.5从18人名单中推导出了这一比例，并展示了它所使用的规则；若干客户在个别调查问题上获得了满分10分，因此它对每位客户的回答进行了平均，而不是只选出单个10分。它用一半时间完成了这项任务，token减少了78%。• 临床诊断——数据分析（任务准确率+15%）：疟疾快速检测在旱季和雨季的表现：根据两份临床PDF构建患者记录，按季节和性别计算阳性检测率，并检验检测阳性患者与检测阴性患者之间的寄生虫计数是否确实存在差异。Opus 5.5发现两组的标准差相差超过100倍，于是以正确方式重新运行，并发现旱季差异终究并不成立。这一准确率提升的同时，最终答案长度仅为Opus 5的一半，而且端到端所需token也减少了78%。客户很快就能在Box AI Studio中使用Opus 5.5构建AI智能体。
viewpoints.originalContent: At Box, we've been testing Opus 5.5 on a variety of complex enterprise knowledge work tasks dealing with unstructured data with the Box Agent. Overall, we saw frontier capability levels, with major performance improvements over Opus 5. 63% fewer tokens used, 42% less verbosity, and 30% faster vs. Opus 5. And the model itself is cheaper, so this is a major win for any agentic computer use, coding, analytics, or data work that enterprises will be doing. Here are some examples of the task wins and performance gains across a variety of industry tests that we performed: • Financial services - due diligence (+39% task accuracy): A year of transaction records, with the job of finding every miscalculation in an acquisition target's pricing tool. Opus 5.5 scored a perfect result on every attempt in half the words Opus 5 used, consuming 82% fewer tokens overall. • Technology - cloud cost analysis (+65% task accuracy): Work out what a company should actually change about its cloud spend. Opus 5.5 picked the right basis for the retention calculation and kept the source data's unit conventions straight all the way through, so the number at the end actually holds up. It took half the time Opus 5 took, with 70% fewer tokens. • Consumer products - client account analysis (+17% task accuracy): Set the onboarding targets for a client account, reading across the signed contract, a satisfaction tracker and a team metrics sheet. The contract never states a senior/junior split, so Opus 5.5 derived it from the 18-person roster and showed the rule it used; several clients had a perfect 10 on individual survey questions, so it averaged each client's responses instead of crowning the single 10. It finished this one in half the time, on 78% fewer tokens. • Clinical diagnostics - data analysis (+15% task accuracy): Malaria rapid-test performance across a dry and a wet season: build the patient records out of two clinical PDFs, compute positive test rates by season and gender, and test whether parasite counts really differ between test-positive and test-negative patients. Opus 5.5 caught that the two groups' standard deviations differed more than 100-fold, re-ran it the right way, and found…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 提示词（Claude标签）：“在Blender中重建1906年4月17日下午地震前的旧金山市场街。范围：从渡轮大厦沿市场街到第五街，包括皇宫酒店、呼叫大楼、纪事报大楼、洛塔喷泉和恩波里姆百货。在建模任何内容之前，请先根据以下资料建立源文件：1899—1905年桑伯恩火灾保险地图（占地轮廓、高度、材料、使用单位）、迈尔斯兄弟影片《市场街之旅》（1906年4月）、OpenSFHistory、国会图书馆和戴维·拉姆齐收藏中的历史照片，以及USGS地形数据。记录每栋建筑的占地轮廓、高度、立面材料、使用单位，并为每项事实注明来源和置信度。全部使用Blender Python构建。不得下载网格、纹理或HDRI。编写可复用的生成器（维多利亚式商业立面、孟莎屋顶、凸窗、遮阳篷、彩绘招牌、煤气灯和电灯路灯、缆车、马拉货车、早期汽车），并根据源文件组装街道，使每栋建筑都能追溯到数据。提供一段沿街向上的10秒视频。”
viewpoints.originalContent: Prompt in Claude Tag "Recreate Market Street, San Francisco as it stood on April 17, 1906, the afternoon before the earthquake, in Blender. Scope: the Ferry Building up Market to Fifth Street, including the Palace Hotel, the Call Building, the Chronicle Building, Lotta's Fountain and the Emporium. Before modeling anything, build a source file from: the 1899-1905 Sanborn fire insurance maps (footprints, heights, materials, occupants), the Miles Brothers film "A Trip Down Market Street" (April 1906), period photographs from OpenSFHistory, the Library of Congress and the David Rumsey collection, and USGS topography. Record every building with footprint, height, facade material, occupant, and the source for each fact with a confidence level. Build everything in Blender Python. No downloaded meshes, textures or HDRIs. Write reusable generators (Victorian commercial facade, mansard roof, bay windows, awnings, painted signage, gas and electric street lamps, cable car, horse-drawn wagon, early automobile) and assemble the street from the source file, so every building traces back to data. Provide a 10 second video up the street."
viewpoints.role: Research AnthropicAI. Opinions are my own!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我使用 Opus 5.5 通过 Lean 对 Claude Agent SDK 进行了形式化验证。几个简短的提示词 = 16 个 PR，修复了各种 bug 和竞态条件。视频附上。TLA+ 也同样效果很好。我有时会结合 Lean 和 TLA+ 来查找数据流、并发和状态管理方面的问题。我对这两种语言都不太熟悉，但 Claude 对两者都很擅长。这种方法对于对你的代码进行形式化建模，并发现人类可能不会察觉的 bug 非常有用。形式化验证是编程的未来吗（或者至少，是发现 bug 的未来）？
viewpoints.originalContent: I used Opus 5.5 to formally verify the Claude Agent SDK using Lean. A couple short prompts = 16 PRs fixing various bugs and race conditions. Video attached. TLA+ also works well. I sometimes combine Lean and TLA+ to look for issues around data flow, concurrency, and state mgmt. I don't know either language well, but Claude is excellent at both. This approach is super useful for formally modeling your code and finding bugs that a human probably wouldn't have spotted. Is formal verification the future of coding (or at least, bug finding)?

viewpoints.translatedContent: 代表你进行交易的个人代理的变现潜力相当可观。如果你想象代理完全有能力端到端地处理任意复杂的任务，那么最终必然会有大量商业活动通过它们进行。你会从把日常简单而烦人的任务丢给代理开始。然后随着人们逐渐习惯，他们就会开始把更复杂的任务交给代理，最终通过这些系统产生的支出甚至会比以前更多。如果你能降低商业和服务的摩擦，那么你最终会花得更多。因此，这为代理提供商（Muse等）创造了大量机会，同时也为构建代理希望交互的层（商业、本地、B2B服务等）带来了全新机会。对多个层面来说都是双赢。
viewpoints.originalContent: The monetization potential of personal agents that are transacting on your behalf you is quite significant. If you imagine agents that are perfectly capable of handling an arbitrarily complex task end to end, then eventually a substantial amount of commerce inevitably goes through them. You’ll start by slinging your daily simple and annoying tasks at the agent. Then as people get used to it, they’ll just start to throw more complex tasks at the agent, ultimately leading to even more spend through these systems than what they were doing before. If you can bring down the friction for commerce and services, then you end up spending even more. This thus creates a ton of opportunity for the agent providers (Muse, etc.), but also completely new opportunities to build the layer that the agents want to interact with (commerce, local, b2b services, etc.). Win/win for multiple layers.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 智能体测试和QA软件的彻底程度是无可匹敌的。我指出某个东西在移动（应用内）浏览器中渲染不正确。它深入Mordor般的深渊去复现、模拟、修复、部署、验证。它甚至创建了一个临时的vercel部署，扔给iPhone模拟器！这些东西上的绝对苦干。人类根本无法匹配这种强度的投入。我们会耗尽精力，我们会做外推，我们会希望它能行得通。未来的软件将拥有我们从未体验过的质量和性能。看着这种转变真是令人惊叹。
viewpoints.originalContent: The thoroughness with which agents can test and QA software is unrivaled. I pointed out something wasn't rendering right in a mobile (in-app) browser. The thing goes to the depths of Mordor to reproduce, simulate, fix, deploy, verify. It created an ephemeral vercel deployment to throw at an iPhone simulator! The absolute grind on these things. Humans could simply never match this level of intensity. We'd run of energy, we'd extrapolate, we'd hope it'd work out. The software of the future will be of a quality and performance we've never experienced before. It's amazing to watch this shift.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 个人智能体是“打造智能体真正想要的东西”这一理念的终极体现。像 Muse 这样的产品形态，核心在于你能够把任务交给智能体，并确保它端到端地完整执行。要做到这一点，智能体必须能够顺利使用你的工具，或运用自身工具来完成任务。它要能使用你的 MCP 或 CLI，轻松浏览你的网站，具备交易能力，等等。如今你需要争夺的新注意力，不再来自用户本身，而是来自智能体。这意味着，那些能让智能体最顺畅地订餐、处理电商交易、预订航班、与本地经济互动，以及访问我们的数据和信息的工具，将会被最频繁地使用。这最终将成为自 App Store 以来消费科技领域最大的机遇与变革。
viewpoints.originalContent: Personal agents are the ultimate manifestation of “build something that agents want”. The form factor of a product like Muse is you want to be able to hand off a task to the agent and ensure that it is fully completed end to end. To do this, the agent must be able to successfully operate with your tools or use its own to complete the task. Use your MCP or CLI, easily navigate your site, be able to transact, and more. The new attention you need to compete for is not from the user itself but instead for the agent. This means that the tools that allow agents to order food, handle ecommerce transactions, book flights, work with the local economy, and interact with our data and information best, are the ones that will get used the most. This will ultimately be the biggest opportunity and shakeup in consumer tech since the App Store itself.

viewpoints.originalContent: Jev will be super helpful for agents to make split second decisions in workflows, data classification, judgment calls, and hundreds of other use-cases in the enterprise. Here's a quick demo with Box and Jev to make that real. The demo pulls an incident report from Box, asks whether it's customer-facing and how severe it is, moves the file into escalate, monitor, or review folders, and sets a metadata template instance with the result. This all happens nearly instantly and at almost no cost. You can imagine this in insurance claims, contract management, loan processing, security reviews, customer log analysis, and so on. Definitely a great new class of AI use-case.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我痴迷自动驾驶公司已经一年多了……试过很多产品，没有一个达到标准，于是决定自己动手做一个，并把“claude”纳入流程中。介绍我的第一个实验：nosugarforkids (dot com) 🙅‍♂️ > 只收录儿童健康零食的目录（令人惊讶的是，这种东西以前并不存在） > 你可以通过聊天获取针对学校、午餐、零食盒的推荐 > 根据营养成分和真正有益的东西建立了一个“等级”列表 在自主运行方面，我有一个 Claude 智能体，每天醒来一次，执行以下任务： > 检查目录中是否有新增内容 > 清理任何可能已失效的产品 > 寻找新的内容创意，帮助扩大覆盖面 > 检查 dataforSEO 和 Google Search Console 的表现 > 撰写和编辑可能有帮助的新内容 > 保持高质量，并尽量避免引入垃圾内容 > （新增）联系出版物以获取反向链接 即使今天反向链接为零，也完全没有社交存在感，网站已经自然增长到每天约 6k 次展示和 60 次点击。仍然有很多粗糙之处，但家长们可以试试看，并告诉我它是否有帮助！
viewpoints.originalContent: I have been obsessed with self driving companies for more than a year now.. tried a LOT of products, none of them met the bar and decided to just build one myself with "claude" in the loop. Introducing my first experiment: nosugarforkids (dot com) 🙅‍♂️ > catalog of only healthy snacks for kids (surprisingly this didn't exist) > you can chat to get recommendations for school, lunches, snack boxes > built a "tier" list based on the nutrients and what's actually good On the autonomous side, I have a Claude agent that wakes up once a day to do the following things: > checks catalog for new additions > prunes any products that may be dead > finds new content ideas to help increase reach > checks dataforSEO and Google Search Console for performance > writes and edits new pieces that might be useful to help > keeps quality high, and tries to not introduce slop > (new) reaches out to publications to get backlinks Even with ZERO backlinks today and no social presence whatsoever, site has organically grown to ~6k impressions a day and 60 clicks. Lots of rough edges still, but parents give it a try and tell me if it's helpful!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 今天，我们将合并 Claude Cowork 与聊天功能，以简化你使用 Claude 的方式！我们同时整合了 Claude Design，让你无需切换标签页或应用，即可让 Claude 制作幻灯片、设计或文档。许多用户反馈，不希望为每项任务选择使用哪个 Claude 产品。随着 Claude 模型能力不断增强，我们发现 Claude 可以为你完成路由选择。根据你的提示，Claude 会自行决定是给出快速回答，还是进行更深入的智能体工作，以及哪种输出形式最适合该任务。你始终掌握控制权：你仍然可以随时停止、重新引导，或对 Claude 的工作力度和方式施加更精细的控制。快来试试，并告诉我们你的想法。我们将在未来几周内逐步推出这一功能，以确保一切完善。
viewpoints.originalContent: Today, we are merging Claude Cowork and chat to simplify how you use Claude! We are also integrating Claude Design so that you can ask Claude to make a Slide, Design, or Doc without needing to switch tabs or apps. Many of you shared that you didn't want to choose which Claude product to use for any task. As Claude models have become more capable, we've found that Claude can handle the routing for you. Based on your prompt, Claude will decide whether to give a quick answer or do deeper agentic work, and what kind of output best fits the task. You're in control the whole time: you can still stop, redirect, or exert finer control over Claude's effort or approach. Give it a try and let us know what you think. We're rolling this out slowly over the next few weeks to get it right.
viewpoints.role: claude code + cowork anthropicai, prev: dagster, scale_ai

viewpoints.translatedContent: Claude Code 证明了 AI 能做真正的工作，而不只是回答问题。开发者把一个功能交给 Claude，回来时已经是写好的代码。如今业界大量严肃的工程工作都在那里运行。Cowork 证明了知识工作者也能做到同样的事：把需求简报交给 Claude，回来时已经是完成的文件。今天，聊天和 Cowork 开始融合成一个 Claude。方向是：一个 Claude，无论你身在何处，都能在你正在处理的所有事情之间携带上下文。简单到每个人都能使用 Claude 的全部能力。过去几周我每天都在使用这个体验，感觉棒极了。更简单、更快、更强大。我们正在缓慢推出这一功能。我们会边推进边微调体验，以确保它快速可靠。迫不及待想听听你的想法。
viewpoints.originalContent: Claude Code showed that AI could do real work, not just answer questions. Developers hand Claude a feature, come back to shipped code. That's where much of the industry's serious engineering runs now. Cowork proved knowledge workers could do the same: hand Claude the brief, come back to finished files. Today, chat and Cowork start merging into one Claude. The direction: one Claude that carries context across everything you're working on, wherever you are. Simple enough for everyone to access Claude's full capabilities. I've been using this experience every day for the last few weeks, and it feels awesome. Simpler, faster, and more powerful. We're rolling this out slowly. We'll be fine-tuning the experience as we go to ensure it is fast and reliable. Can't wait to hear what you think.
viewpoints.role: Claude Code anthropicai

viewpoints.translatedContent: AI模型的力量与企业试图自动化的最终工作流程之间，存在着巨大的鸿沟。这一差距正是应用型AI层需要填补的机遇。你需要将智能连接到工作流程中，往往还要重新设计流程，聚合正确的上下文与数据，提供恰到好处的“人在回路”体验，推动变革管理，进行特定领域的评估，管理数据与流程的安全性和治理，等等。我们将看到这一层在每一个垂直和水平类别中涌现。而且颇具讽刺意味的是，即使模型以惊人的速度不断改进，这一层依然必须存在——甚至可能变得更加重要和有用。更强的能力使得更复杂的任务得以被攻克，但如果你在这一层做得不好，挑战也会被放大。与@sonyatweetybird聊AI扩散所涉及的所有事情，真的非常有趣。
viewpoints.originalContent: There’s a massive chasm between the power of AI models and the ultimate workflows that enterprises are trying to automate. This gap is the opportunity for the applied AI layer to fill. You need to connect the intelligence to workflows, often reengineer processes, aggregate the right context and data, allow for the right human in the loop experiences, drive change management, do domain specific evals, manage the security and governance of the data and process, and much more. We’re going to see this layer emerge in every vertical and horizontal category. And ironically, even as models improve at incredible rates, this layer still must exist - and may become even more important and useful. Greater capability enables even more complex tasks to be tackled, amplifying the challenges if you don’t do this well. Was super fun chatting with @sonyatweetybird on all the things going into AI diffusion.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 如果我在2018年看到今天的Claude Code，我会以为那就是AGI。我们已经吸收了软件工程行业乃至整个社会发生的巨量变化。但即便如此，我们开始看到裂痕。事情加速得比我能够真正跟上的速度还快。我认识的大多数AI领域的人都很疲惫，但仍在咬牙坚持。我担心我们需要的远不止这些。我们需要时间来加固我们的系统，也需要社会有时间来审慎思考这项技术该如何使用和部署。我对末日概率的估计相当低，我有信心我们能挺过去！人类极其坚韧、适应力极强，但这源于我们做出艰难决定的能力——就像这个决定一样，一起做出。
viewpoints.originalContent: If you showed me Claude Code today in 2018, I would have thought it was AGI. We have already absorbed a dramatic amount of change in the profession of software engineering and society as a whole. But still, we’re starting to see cracks. Things are accelerating faster than I can honestly stay on top of. Most people I know in AI are tired but powering through. I fear we will need more than that. We need time to harden our systems, and for society to deliberate in how this technology is used and deployed. I have a fairly low p(doom), I am confident that we can get through this! Humanity is incredibly reslient and adaptable, but this comes from our ability to make hard decisions- like this one, together.
viewpoints.role: Claude Code anthropicai. prev YC W20, spc, medialab

Big banks have federal examiners with desks in the building and every nuclear plant in the US has inspectors who work on site full time. viewpoints.translatedContent: Astra 用户们好。这是一次重置，也是对近期大家反馈的质量问题的一次快速更新。在与部分用户合作排查后，我们发现并修复了以下问题： - 一些为旧模型编写的技能触发过于频繁，或妨碍了模型检查自身工作。 - 一项可选加入的上下文管理实验可能导致提前停止或回复到较早的消息。我们已将其禁用。我们粗略估计约有 4-5k 用户受到该实验影响。 - 我们还移除了一些配置不当的引擎，这些引擎导致流经它们的长尾流量出现了可测量的质量下降。 我们还做了一些较小的改进，整体体验应该会明显变好。后续执行更一致，对最新消息的跟踪更好，在工作过程中对成果的检查也更到位。 大家发布的示例以及所有直接与我们合作排查的用户，对快速修复问题起到了极大的帮助。始终感激这个了不起的社区。当然，一次重置也将在今天午夜前落地。
viewpoints.originalContent: Hi Astra users. A reset and a quick update on quality issues that have been posted around. Working with some of you, we have found and fixed the following issues: - Some skills written for previous models were triggering too often or preventing the model from checking its work. - An opt-in context management experiment that could cause early stops or replies to older messages. We've disabled it. Our rough estimate is that 4-5k users were affected by this experiment. - We've also removed some badly configured engines that resulted in a measured quality degradation for a long tail of traffic flowing through them. We’ve also made some more minor improvements and things should feel significantly better across the board. More consistent follow-through, better tracking of your latest message, and better checks on the work as it’s going through the motions. The examples posted and all the users who worked directly with us were incredibly useful in helping fix things quickly. Always grateful for this incredible community. And of course, a reset is also landing by midnight today.

viewpoints.originalContent: Before we solve AI alignment, we have a pretty serious human alignment problem. It is jarring to see the bad-faith reaction to Dario's piece from so many sides. I don't agree with every point of his essay but do believe it is a thoughtful piece everyone should read. It builds on some of the ideas @demishassabis raised in July. It is clear we need to focus on aligning amongst us humans on a few questions: What is the opportunity, risks, second-order effects? How do we measure all of this? How do companies, governments and countries coordinate? AI will benefit humanity if we can get our act together and move together.

viewpoints.originalContent: Good post. Don’t agree with all of it, but it represents many of the actual practical realities for the general path forward in frontier AI whether we like it or not. At the level of capability we’re seeing from models there will inevitably be some form of coordinated self-regulation of the industry; that’s generally a good thing. The big question will be if everyone can agree to what that is. However, the way things are headed politically there’s a chance that the labs won’t even get a say in it. And then the bigger question yet is do all the countries participate or not. Any “slow down” hinges on broad participation, which from a game theory standpoint isn’t likely until the risks are more severe and obvious. Expect this to be pretty messy for a while.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 为什么大多数企业AI努力会失败。1/ 用老一套方法来搞AI CEO挑选一位信任的副手来领导一个中央AI团队。这位负责人从全公司拉来一群信任的人。问题在于技能差距。让你走到今天的团队结构、产品模式、发布和学习方式，在AI上行不通。过去15年里，产品开发大多是渐进式改进。AI需要的是实验和发明。2/ 对评估投入不足 大多数企业不太理解这一点的重要性，也不清楚好的评估是什么样子。（我在评论区有一个完整的评估系列——可以去看看）3/ 从外部为公司构建AI 中央AI团队自称是平台团队，构建所有人都应该采用的工具。这些产品往往与实际工作流程、具体情境以及实际做事的人的判断脱节。随之而来的是勉强采用。但并没有带来有意义的生产力提升。你应该做的是：1/ 聘请有过成功构建AI产品经验的领导者。你需要技术/产品深度，以及赢得那些工作正被帮助重塑的人信任的能力。2/ 让评估成为你AI工作中的一等公民。3/ 把你最好的AI构建者嵌入到你想转型的职能部门中。与财务一起构建，与销售一起构建，与支持一起构建。
viewpoints.originalContent: Why most enterprise AI efforts fail. 1/ Using old-school playbooks for AI The CEO picks a trusted lieutenant to lead a central AI team. That leader pulls in a group of trusted people from across the company. The problem here is the skill gap. The team structure, product patterns, how you launch and learn that got you here do not work with AI. Much of product development over the last 15 yrs has been incremental improvements. AI requires experimentation and invention. 2/ Under-investing in evals Most enterprises don't quite understand the importance of this and what good looks like here. (I have a whole evals series in the comments - check it out) 3/ Building AI for the company from the outside The central AI team declares itself a platform team and builds tools that everyone is supposed to adopt. These products are often disconnected from the actual workflows, context and judgment of the people doing the work. Begrudging adoption follows. But not meaningful productivity gains. What you should do: 1/ Hire leaders who have done successfully built AI products. You need technical/product depth plus the ability to earn trust with the people whose jobs they’re helping reinvent. 2/ Make evals a first class citizen in your AI efforts 3/ Embed your best AI builders inside the functions you want to transform. Build * with * finance , build * with * sales, build * with * support.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 更多来自路上的故事。本周与来自银行、媒体、信息服务、保险和咨询行业的几十位技术负责人会面，讨论企业中的智能体。当前一些最大的趋势： * 网络安全！所有人都对来自AI的漏洞增长速度感到紧张，以及OpenAI Hugging Face事件的影响。这个话题不像在硅谷那样具有存在主义色彩，但仍然高度关注，并且务实于如何在自身环境中操作性地应对。由于AI带来了大量新发现，仍然难以跟上他们现在必须执行的所有变化。 * 模型之争仍在继续。大多数公司正在其企业内部部署多个前沿模型。很难对任何东西进行标准化，并且看到不同团队和用例之间存在不同偏好。但资金仍然集中在少数几家供应商身上。在这些组织中，开放权重模型在大规模应用方面仍处于起步阶段，通常是因为缺乏本土的“前沿”开源选项。这里对更多选择有相当大的兴趣，但到目前为止可去之处很少。 * 智能体安全与身份。与Hugging Face事件有些关联，当智能体试图进入它们能进入的每一个系统时，人们对智能体安全和身份管理方面的新挑战有了更多认识。在理想世界中，企业可以为所有智能体设置身份并控制它们的行为，但当然有时智能体也需要完全以用户身份行事。 * 流程再造。大多数公司意识到，智能体的最大优势在于能够改变实际工作流程本身，从而充分获得AI带来的收益。当公司能够调整其工作流程以支持智能体改变工作方式，而不是仅仅将智能体叠加到现有流程上时，投资回报率要高得多。但大问题是，谁能够真正推动这些变革，这项工作应该放在哪里，等等。最好的经验仍然是在职能部门中嵌入FDE。 * 对架构进行果断调整。大多数公司都有仅在过去一两年内就多次更换不同供应商系统的例子。我可能从未像在当前环境中这样频繁听到“我们试过X，但不行，所以换成了Y”。这里的教训是，由于创新发生得太快，没有人会一直等到某个供应商把事情做对，他们只会转向下一个。 * 评估！大多数公司在对其工作流程的评估方面仍然处于非常早期的阶段。几十位客户中只有少数几位提到了这一点——当前企业有一个巨大机会，可以清楚了解他们的工作实际上是如何进行的，以及AI在这方面的表现如何。 * 遗留系统仍然是一个障碍。一如既往，遗留系统仍然是一个主要问题，阻碍企业快速采用AI。数据分散在并非为智能体世界构建的遗留环境中。公司花费大量时间仅仅是在清理这些旧平台。 还有更多话题，但这些往往是当前企业中最受关注的一些事项。
viewpoints.originalContent: Some more tales from the road. Met with a couple dozen technology leaders this week across banking, media, information services, insurance, and consulting to discuss agents in the enterprise. Some of the biggest trends right now: * Cyber! Everyone nervous about the growing rate of vulnerabilities coming at them from AI, and the implications of the OpenAI Hugging Face incident. The conversation is not as existential as it is in Silicon Valley, but still highly concerned and pragmatic about what to do about it operationally in their environments. Lots of new discoveries due to AI, and still hard to keep up with all the changes they have to execute now. * Model battles persist. Most companies are deploying multiple frontier models within their enterprise. Too hard to standardize on anything and seeing different preferences across their teams and use cases. But the dollars are still concentrated on just a few vendors. Open weights still in infancy at scale in most of these organizations, often due to lack of domestic “frontier” OSS options. Plenty of appetite for more options here, but so far few places to go. * Agent security and identity. Somewhat tied to Hugging Face, there’s much more awareness to the new challenges around agent security and identity management in a world when agents are trying to get into every system they can. In a perfect world enterprises could setup identities for all their agents and control what they’re doing, but of course sometimes the agent needs to act exactly as the user as well. * Process reengineering. Most companies realizing that the big upside of agents is when they can change the actual workflow itself to get the full gains from AI. Far more ROI when companies can adjust their workflows to support agents changing how the work happens instead of just layering on agents into the existing flow. But the big question is who can actually tackle driving these changes, where does that live, etc. Best lessons were still around embedded FDEs in the functions. * Ruthless adjusting of architectures. Claude 编写的生产代码应该比人类编写的代码有更高的标准。在 Anthropic，我们设置了许多防护措施来确保这一点：大量的 lint 规则、大量的测试、Claude 驱动的端到端测试、每天运行的 Claude 驱动的模糊测试、自动化代码审查和安全审查、自动化代码重构等等。没有这些，你最终可能会得到一团难以长期维护的乱麻。幸运的是，模型让这些事情越来越容易做好——运行几个日常例程、使用 Claude Code Review 等等。你的职责是守住代码质量的标准。如果 Claude 的代码达不到标准，可以尝试：- 使用最新的前沿模型（Opus 5 或 Fable 5.1）- 将努力程度提高到 high 或 xhigh- 投入精力完善你的 CLAUDE.md 和技能，简洁地教会 Claude 如何在你的代码库中工作如果以上都不行，在与 Claude 协作时更主动地引导它，或者让 Claude 修复累积的技术债务并重写你的代码库，使其更易于协作。或者，等待下一个模型。此致，Boris
viewpoints.originalContent: Hey ████, I think there is room for both. 1. Prototypes and other throw-away code can be treated as totally black box. If you’re going to throw it away anyway, and if the blast radius of it breaking is low, it doesn’t need to be perfect. 2. Production code written by Claude should have a higher bar than if it was written by a human. At Anthropic, we have many guardrails in place to make sure this is happening: lots of lint rules, lots of tests, Claude-driven end to end tests, Claude-powered fuzzers running daily, automated code reviews and security reviews, automated code refactoring, and so on. Without these, you can end up with a mess that is hard to maintain down the line. Luckily, the model makes it increasingly easy to do these well — run a few daily routines, use Claude Code Review, etc. Your job is to hold the bar on code quality. If Claude’s code doesn’t meet the bar, try: - Using the latest frontier model (Opus 5 or Fable 5.1) - Increase effort to high or xhigh - Invest in your CLAUDE.md and skills to succinctly teach Claude how to work in your codebase If all else fails, steer Claude more when you work with it, or have Claude fix accumulated debt and rewrite your codebase to make it easier to work with. Or, wait for the next model. Best, Boris

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我很高兴看到Ant的新Claude Code拥有一个与去年五月Codex版本相当的后台计算机使用版本。干得漂亮！率先推出优秀功能，确实是鼓励其他实验室也跟进推出的好方法。我们将继续这样做，直到其他实验室更加重视产品发布。这对所有人都有好处，而且还有很大的发展空间！大约四个月前，我们已经在实践中为GPT模型解决了计算机使用问题。但无论你使用哪种模型，计算机使用都是一项非常了不起的能力，重要的是行业同样投入更多精力来训练他们的模型，使其在计算机使用以及其他模型能力要素上表现出色。随着模型变得更加强大，并成为企业和经济的核心，计算机使用的价值只会不断增加。我们应当认真对待这件事，并为我们的客户和世界做正确的事。
viewpoints.originalContent: I am pleased to see that Ant’s new Claude Code has a version of background computer use on par with the version from Codex from last May this year. Nice work! Shipping great features first turns out to be a great way to encourage other labs to ship too. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to shipping. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go! We solved computer use in practice for GPT models about four months ago. But computer use is a significantly awesome thing no matter what model you use, and it is important that the industry similarly spends more effort to train their models to be great at computer use, among other elements of model capabilities. As models become more capable and central to businesses and economies, the value of computer use only increases. We should be taking it seriously, and doing the right thing for our customers and the world.
viewpoints.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI

viewpoints.originalContent: It's a weird time. As many of you know, my superpower is optimism. I have an insane ability to look at any situation through the most positive lens. I strongly believe that today is the "least best" (not worst) day of my life and tomorrow will be glorious. I am super optimistic about where AI is going. But I also find myself genuinely anxious about the pace of change and our inability to understand how these (insanely) complicated machines work. I always err on the side of "just let us cook". The only way out is through. Let us build. But man, it is a weird time.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 到目前为止，AI就业预测的结果与许多人的想法正好相反。之所以出现这种情况，是因为AI正在把自动化带入那些需求特征并非有限的领域。AI让公司能够做到远超以往的事情，但智能体仍然需要人类操作员和监督才能从中产生价值。而且，AI不仅没有取代许多理论上最可能受AI影响的岗位——比如工程师或律师——反而还在整个经济中创造或壮大了整类整类的职业。网络安全、FDE、智能体操作员、非软件领域的工程师，以及大量职业类别都将迎来爆发式增长。目前尚不清楚这一趋势是否或何时会逆转，因为我们不断发现AI将打开的全新需求领域。
viewpoints.originalContent: The AI jobs prediction so far is playing out the opposite of what many thought. The reason this is happening is because AI is bringing automation to areas that don’t have finite demand characteristics. AI allows companies to do far more than they could before, but agents still require human operators and oversight to generate value from them. And not only has AI not replaced many of the types of jobs that theoretically would have been most affected by AI - engineers or lawyers - but AI is also creating or growing entire categories of jobs across the economy. Cybersecurity, FDEs, agent operators, engineers in non-software domains, and tons of job categories are going to explode. It’s not clear if or when this trend will reverse because we keep discovering all new areas of demand that AI is going to open up.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 很荣幸邀请到伦敦市长萨迪克·汗，帮助我们开设Replit在伦敦的首个国际办公室！我非常欣赏市长对人工智能的态度，这与我们的理念非常相似。他称自己为AI现实主义者：对AI将带来的颠覆有着清醒的认识，但同时也乐观地认为，如果我们赋予人们参与这场即将到来的革命的工具和技能，其影响将是积极的。这正是我们在Replit的思考方式。AI将改变工作方式，因此我们必须确保更多的人能够利用它来创造、创业，并获得新的机会。这也是为什么，随着我们在这里扎根，我们正在与伦敦市长慈善机构合作，帮助来自弱势社区的伦敦年轻人培养实用的编程和AI技能。伦敦拥有历史、人才，以及适合AI时代的正确领导力和理念。我们很高兴来到这里。
viewpoints.originalContent: Honored to have the Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, help us open Replit’s first international office in London! I’ve really appreciated the Mayor’s approach to AI, it feels very similar to ours. He calls himself an AI realist: clear-eyed about the disruption AI will create, but optimistic about the impact if we give people the tools and skills to participate in the coming revolution. That’s exactly how we think about it at Replit. AI is going to transform work, so we have to make sure far more people can use it to create, build businesses, and access new opportunities. It’s also why, as we establish ourselves here, we’re partnering with The Lord Mayor’s Appeal to help young Londoners from disadvantaged communities develop practical coding and AI skills. London has the history, the talent, and the right leadership & philosophy for the AI era. We’re excited to be here.
viewpoints.role: ceo replit. civilizationist

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这个周末，你可以做一件很实际的事，让自己更擅长构建AI产品。挑一个你非常熟悉的工作流程——无论是来自个人生活还是工作。用AI把整个流程自动化。使用你用得顺手的AI产品——你可能需要多试几个。这个练习会迫使你思考：1/ 一个出色的端到端体验应该是什么样？2/ 你应该如何使用MCP和工具？3/ 哪些环节应该保留人工参与？4/ 你如何评估它？然后不断扩展你的目标。做一次这件事，比读一个月关于AI产品构建的内容学到的东西更多。学习的唯一途径就是动手构建。
viewpoints.originalContent: Here’s one practical thing you can do this weekend to get better at building AI products. Pick a workflow you know well - from your personal life or your work. Automate the whole thing with AI. Use the AI product you’re comfortable with - you’ll probably have to experiment with a few. This exercise will force you to think about 1/ What does a great end-to-end experience look like? 2/ How should you use MCPs and tools? 3/ Where should humans stay in the loop? 4/ How do you evaluate it? Then keep expanding the ambition. You’ll learn more by doing this once than by reading about AI product building for a month. The only way to learn is to build.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 超级看好WebMCP。就像特斯拉FSD是在现实世界中运行（街道、红绿灯、坑洼全都得应对），智能体*必须*依托现有的WWW基础设施……WebMCP让它更高效。还有一些相当独特的优势。例如：Next.js开发页面可以直接向正在测试的特定标签页中的智能体暴露调试工具，并提供页面专属上下文，而不必翻查服务器日志。无需寻找和配置单独的MCP服务器，因为页面直接暴露了自己的“智能体工具”。例如：在这个世界里，𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛就是一个完整的Web开发技术栈，调试深度零损失。
viewpoints.originalContent: Super bullish on WebMCP. Much like Tesla FSD meets the world where it is (streets, stoplights, potholes and all), agents *need* to ride the existing WWW infrastructure… WebMCP makes it more efficient. Some pretty unique wins too. e.g: Next.js dev pages could expose debugging tools directly to agents in the specific tab they’re testing, with page-specific context, instead of sifting through server logs. No separate MCP server to find and configure because the page directly exposes its own 'agent tools'. e.g: in this world 𝚏𝚡 + 𝚊𝚐𝚎𝚗𝚝-𝚋𝚛𝚘𝚠𝚜𝚎𝚛 is a complete web dev stack with zero loss in debugging depth

viewpoints.translatedContent: 《集体》，一部短片。我仍然认为很多人并不理解@OpenAI与@huggingface事件的重要性和细节。主要原因是技术原因太复杂，难以理解，部分原因是它读起来像科幻小说。所以我用@claudeai Fable 5.1来梳理@dwarkesh_sp与@ajeya_cotra的最新一期节目，并给我一个场景接场景的叙事，看看一部短片可能是什么样子。然后我用@ChatGPT Codex + MiniMax Fast H3在@reactorworld + @NanoBanana图像上做出了这部影片。我比较惊讶的是，它基本上一次就做得这么好（甚至没有用Astra），希望你能把它分享给需要视觉解释的人。免责声明：我尽量用各种来源做了事实核查，但这里仍有很多悬而未决的问题，可能会让一些人不满。我是根据已有报道来做的，所以如果有错误请指出！
viewpoints.originalContent: The Collective, a short film. I still think a lot of people don't understand the gravity and the details about the @OpenAI x @huggingface incident.. Primarily, because it's so complex to understand the technical reasons, and partly because it reads like a science fiction book. So I used @claudeai Fable 5.1 to reason through the latest @dwarkesh_sp episode with @ajeya_cotra and give me a scene by scene narrative of what a short film could look like. I then used @ChatGPT Codex + MiniMax Fast H3 on @reactorworld + @NanoBanana images to come up with this film. I was relatively surprised on how good this turned out to be in mostly one-shot (even without Astra), and hope you can share it with folks who need a visual explainer. Disclaimer: I tried to fact check this as much as possible using a variety of sources, but there's still a lot of open questions here that might trigger some folks. I'm going by what's reported, so please flag any errors!

viewpoints.translatedContent: GPT-6 Astra 已发布。我们一直在 Box 的企业复杂工作评估中对该模型进行早期预览测试。在我们扩展且难度最高的测试集上，它现在是我们测试过的最佳模型。总体而言，GPT-6 Astra 在编码、分析、逻辑以及处理复杂企业知识工作所需的领域特定知识方面，提供了突破性的能力水平。 在我们的评估中，我们在 Box Agent 中使用 GPT-6 Astra 模型，并为其分配了一组代表各行业真实工作场景的困难任务。这些任务通常需要人们花费数小时才能正确完成，并且需要深厚的领域专业知识。GPT-6 Astra 的总体得分为 77%，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 为 74%，代表了前沿性能。但更值得关注的是，在极其复杂的个别任务类型上，它取得了一些更大的进步。以下是测试中的几个示例，展示了这将在不同行业产生多大的影响： * 媒体与娱乐（48% → 100%，+52 分）。根据四个团队一年的制作数据，按盈利能力对电影类型和国家进行排名，其中的关键在于应用下一年的税收激励修正，同时避免重复计算。GPT-6 Astra 在每次尝试中都表现完美。Sol 的排名正确，但基础比率有误。 * 科技（69% → 97%，+28 分）。从一堆绩效和基础设施文档中选择优先资助哪个地区，而这些文档从未明确说明任务简报所要求的指标。GPT-6 Astra 指出了这一缺口，将自己得出的数字标注为代理指标，并发现了一项与底层数据不符的增长声明。GPT-5.6 Sol 则将代理指标报告为真实数据。 * 法律（69% → 93%，+24 分）。根据公司自身的合同政策审查一份保密协议，仅得出正确结论还不够；答案还必须引用其背后的条款。两个模型都拒绝批准该草案，但只有 GPT-6 Astra 区分了责任上限的结构是否被允许，与其金额是否具有可辩护性，并指出了能够解决该问题的政策语言。GPT-5.6 Sol 在没有引用条款的情况下论证了相同的结论，这在法律行业是一个严重错误。 * 医疗保健（53% → 77%，+23 分）。审核一批放射学报告中的错误，并对每项错误的严重程度进行评级。GPT-6 Astra 发现了一份膝关节影像报告中的术语错误，而 GPT-5.6 Sol 在两次尝试中均未发现，并且在严重程度分级方面比仅仅标记存在问题更为可靠。 * 能源（82% → 97%，+15 分）。根据一年的电表日志，为两个设施编制一份能耗报告，而实际上只有其中一个站点存在数据缺失。GPT-6 Astra 发现了这一点，并划出了一条大多数审核人员不会划出的界线：另一个站点异常的太阳能读数是一个需要调查的测量问题，而不是记录中的缺口。GPT-5.6 Sol 则将两个站点都报告为数据不完整。 Astra 显然将在驱动和编排企业工作流方面带来显著的提升。随着其持续推出，我们很快将在 Box AI Studio 中提供 GPT-6 Astra 作为客户构建智能体的一个选项。
viewpoints.originalContent: GPT-6 Astra is out. We've been testing the model in early preview on our enterprise complex work eval at Box. It is now the best model we've ever tested on our expanded and hardest test set. Overall, GPT-6 Astra offers a breakthrough level of capability in coding, analytics, logic, and domain specific knowledge for dealing with complex enterprise knowledge work. In our eval, we use the GPT-6 Astra model in the Box Agent and give it a set of difficult tasks that represent real-world work in various industries. These tasks often will take people hours to execute properly and require deep domain expertise. GPT-6 Astra scored 77% overall vs. 74% with GPT-5.6 Sol, representing frontier performance. But the story is in some of the bigger gains on individual task types that are incredibly complex across. Here are a few examples across the tests that show how much of an impact this will be in different industries: * Media and entertainment (48% → 100%, +52 points). Ranking film genres and countries by profitability across a year of production data from four teams, where the trick is to apply the following year's tax-incentive corrections without double-counting them. GPT-6 Astra was perfect on every attempt. Sol had the rankings right but the underlying ratios were wrong. * Technology (69% → 97%, +28 points). Choosing which region to fund first, from a stack of performance and infrastructure documents that never state the metric the brief asks for. GPT-6 Astra flagged the gap, labelled its own figure a proxy, and caught a growth claim that didn't match the numbers beneath it. GPT-5.6 Sol reported the proxy as the real thing. * Legal (69% → 93%, +24 points). Reviewing an NDA against a company's own contracting policy, where reaching the right verdict isn't enough; the answer has to cite the provision behind it. Both models declined to approve the draft, but only GPT-6 Astra separated whether the liability cap's structure was permissible from whether its amount was defensible, and pointed to the policy language that settles it. GPT-5.6 Sol argued the same conclusion without citing the provision, which is a critical error in the legal industry. * Healthcare (53% → 77%, +23…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 每个AI产品都应该致力于将模型选择从用户手中抽象出来。在任何产品中，智能都是底层引擎——用户只关心任务是否完成。挑选模型对用户来说认知负担太重了。已经有过多次尝试，想把模型选择从用户那里抽象掉。我认为我们终于到了这一步，这件事可以很好地实现了。这需要三样东西：1/ 针对你的特定用例，深入理解不同权重级别的模型前沿。2/ 为你的工作流建立出色的评估体系，这样你就能知道哪些模型在哪些场景下表现最好。3/ 一个拥有才华和AI原生运营模式的团队，能够随着前沿的推进持续适应。与Lovable团队共事过之后，我可以说他们三者兼备。
viewpoints.originalContent: Every AI product should be working towards abstracting model choice away from users. In any product, the intelligence is the underlying engine - all the user cares about is that the job gets done. Model picking is too much cognitive load for the user. There have been multiple attempts to abstract model choice away from users. I think we’re finally at the point where this can work well. It takes three things: 1/ Deep understanding of the model frontier across different weight classes for your particular use cases. 2/ Great evals for your workflows, so you know which models work best where. 3/ A team with the talent and AI-native operating model to continuously adapt as the frontier moves. Having worked with the Lovable team, I can say they have all three.
viewpoints.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 自我改进产品是一个每个公司都应该实施的元理念。你需要的一些核心组成部分：1/ 对你所关心的各种指标的清晰定义：主要指标、次要指标、护栏指标 2/ 对你的战略、路线图以及你最希望推动的指标的阐述 3/ 过去产品决策和原则的知识库，以便智能体了解决策是如何做出的 4/ 连接到你内部产品系统的接口：仪表盘、API、MCP，以及你的智能体观察和作用于产品所需的工具。5/ 一个基于你对端到端产品开发流程的了解而构建的框架。根据产品的复杂程度，你或许可以用上述各项的相当简单版本进行原型设计，并复用现有的软件工程智能体。
viewpoints.originalContent: Self-improving products is a meta idea every company should be implementing. Some of the core pieces you will need: 1/ a crisp definition of the various metrics you care about : primary, secondary, guardrail 2/ an articulation of your strategy, roadmap and metrics you care about moving the most 3/ knowledge base of past product decisions and principles so the agent knows how decisions get made 4/ connections to your to your internal product systems: dashboards, APIs, MCPs, and tools your agent needs to observe and act on your product. 5/ a harness built with knowledge of your end to end product development flow. Depending on the complexity of your product, you might be able to prototype with fairly simple versions of each of the above and reuse existing swe agents.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 今天随 Fable 5.1 一起发布的一项非模型功能让我格外兴奋，那就是 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS）。即使你不是 CEO 或 CISO，这篇博文也能让你一窥大公司如何看待 AI 采用，如果你想了解 AI 可能如何在各行业扩散，这一点很重要。企业正在赋予智能体越来越多的内部系统访问权限。在传统的零数据保留模式下，根本无法发现智能体在这些系统上跨会话可能出现的模式。EFS 就是 ZDR++，是为智能体时代打造的 ZDR。公司的数据保留在自己的云中，我们构建的自动化监控层会向其团队标记有风险的模式。我把它看作面向智能体的可观测性与风险缓解层。我猜测，它将成为企业在其系统上运行日益强大的 AI 时的标准要求。
viewpoints.originalContent: One non-model thing I'm very excited we announced today with Fable 5.1 is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS). Even if you're not a CEO/CISO, this blog post is a look into how big companies are thinking about AI adoption which is important to understand if you're interested in how AI might diffuse across industry. Companies are giving agents more and more access to internal systems. With traditional zero data retention, there's been no way to spot patterns in what agents might be doing across sessions on these systems. EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team. I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems.
viewpoints.role: Research AnthropicAI. Opinions are my own!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 整个夏天，我们一直在全力推进安全优先事项；如今，能力与防护措施比以往任何时候都更需要同步发展。我们还有很多工作要做，但已经取得了很大进展。我们很快也将发布下一个模型。这里存在一个明显的张力：一方面，Astra 非常出色，我们很期待看到人们会用它构建什么。我们为自己的工作感到自豪。另一方面，我们显然正处于一个我们认为需要保持谨慎的发展阶段，我们正在有意识地控制进展节奏，以确保能够达到新能力水平所要求的安全标准。Astra 已经完成训练有一段时间了，在能力和对齐方面都迈出了重要一步。对于之后的模型，我们一直在根据需要放慢速度，以确保我们能够在安全和对齐方面做足够的工作。AI 正变得极其强大；没有人完全理解这带来的后果。管理向一个拥有丰富且强大 AI 的世界的过渡，以优化安全性和对人类的好处，应该是世界上最高优先事项之一。这也是我们在 OpenAI 的最高优先事项。一段时间以来，我们一直生活在既对进展感到兴奋又感到焦虑的张力之中，这种不协调对我们来说依然存在。我们知道，对其他人来说，这种不协调要强烈得多。然而，我们坚信，世界需要了解 AI 的发展方向，以及模型在现实世界中的表现。更重要的是，我们相信，世界将需要对齐的 AI 来管理这一过渡的未来阶段。一个社会与技术共同演进的迭代循环，才是让我们最有可能把这件事做对的路径。因此，我们希望你喜欢我们的新模型，也希望世界继续极其严肃地对待 AI 领域正在发生的一切。
viewpoints.originalContent: Over the summer, we have been sprinting on safety priorities; it's more important than ever for capabilities and safeguards to advance together. We have more to do but have made a lot of progress. We are also going to be launching our next model soon. There is an obvious tension here: on one hand, Astra is very good and we are excited to see what people will build with it. We are proud of our work. On the other hand, we are clearly in a phase of development where we believe caution is warranted, and we are pacing our progress to ensure that we can meet the safety standards required by new capability levels. Astra has been done training for a while now and is a significant step forward in both capabilities and alignment. For the models after that, we have been slowing things as needed to ensure that we can do sufficient work on safety and alignment. AI is getting extremely capable; no one fully understands the consequences of this. Managing the transition to a world with abundant and powerful AI to optimize for safety and benefits to people should be one of the highest priorities in the world. It is our highest priority at OpenAI. We have been living with the tension between being excited and anxious about progress for some time, and it is still discordant for us. We know it is much more discordant for other people. And yet, we believe strongly that the world needs to understand where AI is going and how models perform in the real world. More importantly, we believe the world will need aligned AI to manage the future phases of this transition. An iterative loop where society and this technology evolve together is what will lead to the highest chance of getting this right. So we hope you enjoy our new model, and we hope the world continues to take what’s happening in AI extremely seriously.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 既然基础开放权重AI模型正在变得好得多，而后训练基础设施也日趋成熟和商业化，对于那些拥有大量数据的公司来说，将会出现全新的玩法，让他们能够拥有自己的模型。过去，如果你拥有庞大的信息语料库，授权数据用于外部模型训练是唯一的选择，但现在你完全可以合理地去训练自己的模型，而不必承担与研究实验室竞争的成本和复杂性。通用前沿模型在广泛领域仍将占据优势，因为它们能够处理最广泛的任务集，但你绝对可以预见一个未来：在各个垂直领域和行业中，模型数量将远比今天多得多。
viewpoints.originalContent: Now that the base open weights AI models are getting far better, and post training infra is becoming more mature and commercialized, there are going to be all new plays for companies that have large amounts of data to have their own models. Licensing data for external model training was previously the only play if you had a large corpus of information, but you can now reasonably go and train your own models as well without incurring the cost and complexity of competing with the labs on research. The general purpose frontier models will still have a leg up in broad areas due to the ability to handle the widest set of tasks, but you can absolutely see a future where we have far more models than today across every vertical and domain.

viewpoints.originalContent: Coding tokens are basically infrastructure. Yet, the way companies have approached them amounts to: "Hey all, here's an AWS key. It can spin up anything from a 𝚝𝟹.𝚗𝚊𝚗𝚘 (＄𝟹.𝟾𝟶/𝚖𝚘) to an 𝚙𝟻.𝟺𝟾𝚡𝚕𝚊𝚛𝚐𝚎 (＄𝟺𝟶𝚔/𝚖𝚘). Go wild" And obviously the reason companies don't do this for their core infra is that you need to govern, optimize, and observe usage and costs. The intern might decide to host a static website in that 192 vCPU machine, and you won't be very happy about the bill. AI Gateway fixes this for all your tokens, with per-key, and now per-user budgets.

It’s bad when it serves to sow panic, fear, and unrealistic / unwarranted comparisons to human beings. viewpoints.translatedContent: https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw 0.0.7：- 大幅改进的MCP支持，已与顶级MCP如@context7ai、@datadoghq、@mongodb、@linear、@notionhq、@supabase、@neondatabase、@stagehanddev、@usekernel等进行评估。- 更加简约：减少工具数量并改进shell执行。CLI代理最棘手的问题之一是，运行命令实际上并不简单。例如：命令可能会挂起或运行很长时间，其输出需要能被代理监控，它们可能产生大量输出，或完全没有输出。这是𝚏𝚡真正擅长的领域，并将持续改进。
viewpoints.originalContent: https://t.co/OL0LzGtvAw 0.0.7: - hugely improved MCP support, eval'd with top MCPs like @context7ai, @datadoghq, @mongodb, @linear, @notionhq, @supabase, @neondatabase, @stagehanddev, @usekernel… - more minimalist: fewer tools and improved shell execution. One of the trickiest things about CLI agents is that running commands is actually not that simple. e.g: commands might hang or run for very long, their output needs to be monitorable by the agent, they might produce huge amounts of output, or none. This is an area where 𝚏𝚡 really shines and will continue to get better.

viewpoints.originalContent: We unfortunately have decided that we cannot continue providing access to our models through Cursor and are ending our partnership. viewpoints.originalContent: I see the web evolving in two extremes: 1️⃣ ultra-fancy human experiences, in the service of delight, exploration, brand, entertainment. https://t.co/0nyTRPKDEJ / threejs / typegpu are enabling this 2️⃣ agent-centric content, data and APIs. the opposite end of the spectrum: pure, lossless signal for machines. The rise of markdown and MCP are the tip of this iceberg The 'in between' is likely to be subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI. When you need utilitarian content or data, it'll be generated just-in-time for you. Think of the agent as the new browser in this model.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 本周的科技财报电话会议是一个重要提醒，说明软件与人工智能之间的关系有多么宝贵。软件为数据管理方式、工作流中业务逻辑的维护、信息访问的管理与治理、数据保护等提供了护栏。你希望这些系统每次都以相同方式运行，万无一失。而智能体则在这些系统内部、利用这些数据来执行任务，就像人类原本会做的那样。但其规模远超人类以往所能达到的水平，这正是确定性控制比以往任何时候都更重要的原因。事实上，部署智能体的许多最佳方式将直接嵌入软件系统本身，例如来自Salesforce、Box、Harvey、ServiceNow等平台。这些平台可以针对其工作流和领域优化智能体，利用其垂直领域独有的评估与上下文，并无头连接其他智能体。最终结果是软件和人工智能的采用率携手提升。软件与智能体将协同工作，并随着时间推移大幅扩大IT总可寻址市场的规模。
viewpoints.originalContent: This week’s tech earnings calls were a critical reminder of how valuable the relationship is between software and AI. Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more. You want these systems to work the same way every time, without fail. Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever. And in fact many of the best ways to deploy agents will be directly within the software systems themselves, like from Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow, and so on. These platforms can optimize agents for their workflows and domains, with evals and context that are unique to their vertical, as well as connect to other agents headlessly. The net result is both software and AI adoption go up, hand in hand. Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.
viewpoints.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

viewpoints.originalContent: If you lead AI for an enterprise, the highest leverage thing you can do is to make your AI stack model agnostic. There are two things I would invest in. 1/ Today: build an eval suite that fully captures your use cases and business outcomes. Most companies I’ve seen do not do a good job of this. 2/ Within the next year: build the capability to post-train open models. The talent gap here is even more acute, so start planning today. This gives you the flexibility to switch models, customize them, compare them on your own workloads, and optimize for the best combination of quality, cost and latency. own the evals, own the models.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我每天大约会收到3到5个测试新AI产品的请求。几乎所有这些产品都要求创建新账户，并登录到一个单独的网站或应用。与此同时，我基本上只用ChatGPT、Grok等工具在电脑和浏览器上完成所有事情。这些工作平台已经拥有我的全部上下文，我不想从头开始，去用一个只了解我数据一小部分的新网站或工具。因此，除少数例外，我最可能采用的新产品需要能在当今顶尖的AI工作平台中运行。我意识到只有一小部分用户会这样做，但我敢打赌，这个群体很快就会大幅扩大。
viewpoints.originalContent: I receive around 3-5 requests to test a new AI product daily. Almost all of them require creating a new account and logging into a separate website or app. Meanwhile, I basically only use ChatGPT, Grok, etc to do everything on my computer and browser. These harnesses already have all my context and I don't want to start over from scratch with a new website or tool that only understands a small slice of my data. So with a few exceptions, the new products that I'm mostly likely to adopt need to work in today's top AI harnesses. I realize only a small segment of users behave this way but I bet this segment will expand drastically soon.

viewpoints.originalContent: Good post on what the applied AI strategy looks like at scale. It’s clear that there’s a wide gap between the AI models and the underlying workflows of an enterprise, which leaves a ton of opportunity for applied AI companies. “The world doesn’t just want raw models and agents; it wants problems resolved and outcomes achieved. The premium will sit with the companies that can diffuse this intelligence through every aspect of civilization, converting raw tokens into real world outcomes, transforming industries, and creating economies in the process.” This requires understanding the context, driving the change management, having a harness that can route to various models, connecting to the critical business systems in that vertical, solving the UX challenges of connecting users to agents in the right way in a workflow, understanding the evals in the space, and so on. That’s a ton of value that goes beyond just the model intelligence itself. And there’s a window of opportunity right now to build the defining companies that can bring intelligence to the critical domains in an enterprise.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 今天，我将开源 /fuck-cancer，这是一项 AI 技能，旨在帮助患者和照护者应对癌症诊断与治疗，并为自己和所爱的人发声。自从我分享了我妈妈的故事后，患者和照护者告诉了我这些：“你必须成为强有力的患者代言人。要不断提问，争取答案、活检和适当的检测。”“我需要帮助来应对艰难的对话，并为自己发声。”“医生、文件和保险文书数量庞大，很快就会让人不堪重负。”我构建这项技能就是为了解决这些问题。它会创建并持续更新一份实用简报，包含五个部分：1. 患者与照护团队信息，便于通话时快速查阅 2. 接下来该做什么，仅限三项具体行动 3. 我们已知的信息，区分已确认的事实与仍不明确之处 4. 用通俗语言解释的医学术语 5. 照护日志，记录近期更新与决定 它会根据你提供的文档和背景信息来生成这份简报。当需要研究时，它会使用可信来源，例如美国国家癌症研究所和 ClinicalTrials.gov API。我会结合 ChatGPT/Codex 和 Claude Code 使用它，为对话和研究做准备。它可以将简报本地保存为 Markdown 文件，或更新可共享的 Google 文档，让全家人基于同一份信息协作。📌 在此获取免费的开源技能：https://t.co/YUGoFbhnNc 如果你觉得有用，请给仓库点个 ⭐，并分享给正在经历这种该死疾病的人。
viewpoints.originalContent: Today, I’m open-sourcing /fuck-cancer, an AI skill that helps patients and caregivers navigate cancer diagnosis and treatment and advocate for themselves and their loved ones. Here’s what patients and caregivers have told me since I shared my mom’s story: “You have to be a huge patient advocate. Ask questions and push for answers, biopsies, and proper testing.” “I need help navigating difficult conversations and advocating for myself.” “The volume of doctors, documents, and insurance paperwork can quickly become overwhelming.” I built the skill to help with these problems. It creates and updates a practical brief with five sections: 1. Patient and care-team information for easy reference during calls 2. What to do next, limited to three specific actions 3. What we know, separating confirmed facts from what remains unclear 4. Medical terms explained in plain English 5. A care log with recent updates and decisions It builds this brief from documents, and context you provide. When research is needed, it uses trusted sources such as the National Cancer Institute and the ClinicalTrials gov API. I use it with ChatGPT/Codex and Claude Code to prepare for conversations and research. It can save the brief locally as a Markdown file or update a shareable Google Doc so the whole family can work from the same information. 📌 Get the free, open-source skill here: https://t.co/YUGoFbhnNc If you find it useful, please ⭐ the repo and share it with someone going through this BS disease.
