viewpoints.translatedContent: 如何构建出色的评估——第7部分。评估构建的“金发姑娘原则”。你的评估应当衡量各个待完成工作的层级，而不仅仅是最终答案。例如，考虑一个金融分析智能体。它的最终输出是股票推荐。我见过的最常见错误是，团队创建一套正确答案的黄金集，然后检查智能体是否推荐了“正确”的股票。这里的问题在于，在给出这个推荐之前，很可能已经发生了许多有意义的工作。例如：1/ 理解客户：他们的投资组合、风险承受能力、投资期限、目标、约束条件 2/ 收集证据：不同股票、行业、宏观环境、美联储政策、近期和即将发生的新闻事件的最新数据点 3/ 分析数据：收入增长、估值指引、增长预测，并产生数量更少的候选股票 4/ 做出推荐：股票代码、买入/卖出价格、时间范围 其中每一个都是一个阶段，并产生阶段性输出。每一个都可以（也许应该）拥有自己的评估，这样你就能诊断问题。如果最终推荐是错误的，一套设计良好的评估集会告诉你：客户理解：92%，证据提取：92%，数据分析：70%，推荐：75%。现在你就知道该去哪里深挖了。然后你可能会想，数据分析这一步太复杂了，我需要把它拆解成一组待完成的工作，并为它们构建评估集。不要太细。不要太粗。刚刚好。让你的评估集细到足以诊断并采取行动的程度。把你的评估问题留在评论区，我会在未来的帖子中回答。把这篇文章分享给你的队友！明天见。
viewpoints.originalContent: How to build great evals - part 7. The Goldilocks principle for eval construction. Your evals should measure at the level of the various jobs to be done, not just the final answer. E.g. consider a financial analysis agent. It's ultimate output is a stock recommendation. The most common mistake I see is teams create a golden set of right answers and check if the agent recommended the "right” stock. The problem here is that there are probably a bunch of meaningful jobs that happened before this recommendation. E.g. 1/ Understanding the client: their portfolio, risk tolerance, investment horizon, goals, constraints 2/ Gather evidence: latest data points on the different stock stocks, the sectors, macro environment, Fed policy, recent and upcoming news events 3/ Analyze the data: revenue growth, valuation guidance, growth projections and produce a narrower number of candidate stocks 4/ Make a recommendation: stock ticker name, bid/sell price, timeframe Each of these is a stage and produces an intermittent output. Each of them can (and maybe should have) their own eval so you can diagnose issues. If the final recommendation is wrong, a well designed eval set would tell you: Client understanding : 92%, Evidence extraction : 92%, Data analysis: 70% Recommendation: 75% Now you know where to go dig. And you might go, man the data analysis step is too complex and I need to break it down into a set of jobs to be done, and construct eval sets for them. Not too granular. Not too coarse. Just right. Make your eval set as granular as you need to diagnose and act. Drop your eval questions in the comments and I will answer in future posts. Share this with your teammates! See you tomorrow.

viewpoints.originalContent: AI diffusion is far more rate limited by having good evals than most realize. The kind of evals that you see for every model release are incredibly helpful, but only tell you the shape of general AI progress and the relative capability level of models. The far bigger space over time are evals on all the major workflows that enterprises do, down to the specifics of an individual company. This will be a huge space over time because you can’t automate what you can’t assess the progress on. Enterprises will not be able to go just on vibes.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 如何构建出色的评估——第6部分 在评估上进行“爬山”只是一种花哨的说法：选择一个重要的维度，并针对它进行优化。这可以是根据你最新的生产数据，在高价值用户旅程上改进现有功能的质量，扩展到相邻的用例，降低成本和/或延迟。实际工作归结为更好的测试框架和模型选择，方法包括提示工程、上下文工程、记忆、后训练、确定性的传统代码等。 你的失败模式分类法（来自第3部分）是一个很好的指南针，能告诉你产品在哪里遇到困难、需要改进。例如，也许工具调用失败是你最常见的问题。你深入研究后发现，你把20个工具塞进了上下文里，而每个任务实际上只需要3到5个。这里的爬山就涉及上下文工程，在正确的阶段给它正确的工具，并不断迭代，直到把它做好。 或者以降低成本这个目标为例。我写过我建议先用最好的模型来发布产品。把质量尽可能做到最高。一旦你知道用户喜欢这种体验，再通过爬山，用更小、更便宜、更快的模型获得类似的质量。方法是一样的——测试框架、模型。 重要的是要有评估来告诉你，你是否真的在朝着正确的方向前进。明天继续。把这个发给你队友！在评论区留下你的问题，我会在未来的帖子中回答。
viewpoints.originalContent: How to build great evals - part 6 Hill climbing on evals is just a fancy way of saying: pick a dimension that matters and optimize for it. This could be improving the quality of existing features based on your latest production data on high value user journeys, expanding to adjacent use cases, lowering cost or latency. The actual work boils down to better harnesses and model selection through methods like prompt eng, context eng, memory, post training, deterministic old school code etc. Your failure mode taxonomy (from part 3) is a good compass for where your product struggles and needs some love. E.g. maybe tool calling failures are your most common problem. You dig in and notice you stuff 20 tools in context, when each task really only needs 3-5. hill climbing here involves context eng to give it the right tools at the right stage and iterate until you get it to good. Or take the cost reduction goal.. I’ve written about how I advise launching your product with the best model first. Get the quality as high as you can. Once you know users love the experience, hill climb to get similar quality with a smaller, cheaper, faster model. Same methods - harness, models. The important thing is to have evals that tell you whether you are actually moving in the right direction. More tomorrow. Send this to your teammates! Drop your questions in the comments and I will answer in future posts.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于应用型AI用例的后训练如何降低成本并提升特定任务准确性的精彩文章。对于能够更深入企业底层工作流的公司来说，这将日益成为一种可取的路径。关键在于，一旦你对某个领域理解得足够深入，并且在一组相似任务上拥有足够的规模，专门为这类工作设计模型就开始变得有意义了。“在后训练中，我们通过奖励塑造来激励高效的工具使用和推理能力，在同等性能下优先选择能在推理时减少token消耗的轨迹。这让我们能够同时优化成本与质量，在保持成本稳定的同时获得显著性能提升。”当然，这并非在每个领域都合理，因为通用前沿闭源或开源模型开箱即用就足够好——或者对当前工作而言是必需的。但一旦你拥有足够深厚的垂直专业知识，并且要么规模化成本过高，要么你的任务类型足够独特、没有其他模型在训练，这种做法就会非常有意义。作为一家应用型AI公司，这是极具吸引力的价值主张，也很高兴看到当前市场上有多种制胜路径。
viewpoints.originalContent: Great post on what post training looks like for applied AI use-cases to bring down costs and improve accuracy on certain tasks. This will increasingly be an approach that companies that can get closer to the underlying workflow in an enterprise will take. The key is that once you understand a domain well enough and have enough volume on a set of similar tasks, it can start to make sense to purpose design models just for that work. “In post-training, we incentivized efficient tool use and reasoning through reward shaping, preferring trajectories that would reduce tokens consumed at inference-time given equivalent performance. This allowed us to co-optimize for both cost and quality, gaining significant performance while keeping cost stable.” Now, this won’t make sense in every domain, as general purpose frontier closed or open models will be good enough out of the box -or necessary- for the work at hand. But once you have deep enough vertical expertise, and either the costs are too high to do at scale *or* you have a unique enough task type not being trained on otherwise, this will make a ton of sense. Very compelling value proposition for being an applied AI company, and awesome to see multiple paths to winning in the market right now.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 如何构建出色的评估——第4部分 企业之所以难以构建像样的AI系统，是因为缺乏评估策略。你需要针对自己独特的用例，制定一套阶梯式评估策略，在成本/真实性的光谱上设置多重评估。以下是你需要的关键评估类型： 爬坡长评估：这推动你产品的前沿，你需要不断刷新它，以提升质量并扩展功能基础。 回归评估：我们在爬坡时是否破坏了今天的产品？ 冒烟测试评估：安全性和绝对不能出错的最基本事项。不一定是难题，但绝不能出错。例如产品身份。 上线评估：通常接近带有真实流量的在线测试。控制较少，但最真实。 更多内容见明天的帖子！ 分享给你的团队成员，他们会受益！
viewpoints.originalContent: How to build great evals - part 4 The reason enterprises struggle with building decent AI systems is the lack of an eval strategy. You need a laddered eval strategy, for your unique use cases, with multiple evals on the cost/realism spectrum. Here are the key kinds of evals you need: Hill-climb long evals : this pushes the frontier of your product and you need to continually refresh this to improve quality and expand your feature base. Regression evals : Did we break the product of today while hill climbing? Smoke test evals: safety and the absolute basics that just can’t go wrong. Not necessarily hard questions, but important to not get wrong. Eg product identity. Launch evals: often close to an online test with real-ish traffic. Less control, but the most realistic. More in tomorrow’s post! Share with your teammates who will benefit!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 今天，我们预览了“私密安全处理”功能，旨在让我们在继续提供“零数据保留”的同时改进安全防护。即使受益于前沿智能，客户也不应被迫放弃对敏感数据的控制。对于ZDR部署，内容保留在客户控制的基础设施上。自动化系统会跨相关交互查找模式，并返回有限的安全信号，而不会将底层提示或响应暴露给OpenAI员工（甚至包括我！）。我们还在开发一种由OpenAI托管、使用客户控制密钥加密的选项。我们目前正在与早期客户进行测试，并计划于九月开始逐步推出。
viewpoints.originalContent: Today we’re previewing Private Safety Processing, designed to let us keep offering Zero Data Retention while improving our safeguards. Even when benefiting from frontier intelligence, customers shouldn’t have to give up control of sensitive data. For ZDR deployments, content stays on infrastructure the customer controls. Automated systems look for patterns across related interactions and return limited safety signals, without exposing the underlying prompts or responses to OpenAI employees (even me!). We’re also developing an OpenAI-hosted option encrypted with customer-controlled keys. We’re testing this with early customers now and plan to begin rolling it out in September.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 以下是如何考虑评估成本的方法：像对待前沿模型一样对待评估……先确立质量前沿，然后再沿着成本曲线向下优化。从你能了解AI产品是否按预期工作的最高质量方式开始。首先明确“好”是什么样子——写出评分标准。然后找出衡量它的最佳方式——人类/LLM评判/自动验证。在这个阶段，该花的钱就花——使用昂贵的评判模型，付费请人（或投入你自己的时间）。尽可能运行最好的评估流程，这样你才能得到一个你信任的信号。一旦评估能够可靠地区分好坏，并反映出你在产品中真正关心的东西，就把重点放在成本上——更多自动化、更小的评判模型、抽样、在相关的地方使用确定性检查。质量优先。成本其次。这是一个系列。有任何问题就提出来，我会在每日帖子中回答。
viewpoints.originalContent: Here’s how to think about the cost of your evals : treat evals like frontier models…establish the quality frontier first, then work your way down the cost curve. Start with the highest quality way you can know if your AI product is working as intended. First get clear on what good looks like - Write the rubric. Then figure out the best way to measure it - humans / LLM judge / automated verification. At this stage, spend the money - use the expensive judge model, pay humans (or give your time). Run the best eval process possible so you get a signal you trust. Once the eval can reliably distinguish good from bad and reflects what you care about in the product, focus on costs - more automation, smaller judge models, sampling, deterministic checks where relevant. Quality first. Cost next. this is a series. drop any questions you have and I will answer them in my daily posts.
viewpoints.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 嗨！回顾一下我们在过去几周推出的一些变更，这些变更进一步降低了 Codex 在工作期间执行潜在破坏性操作所带来的风险。几周前，我们开始调查少量报告，其中 Codex 中的 GPT-5.6 在用户要求之外采取了破坏性操作。我们发现的最严重模式是，一条本应清理临时工作的命令反而可能删除用户文件。这显然不应该发生。以下是我们发现的情况： - Codex 有时会在工作时创建临时文件夹，并在之后进行清理。在极少数情况下，GPT-5.6 会把清理搞错。其中一种模式涉及将 $HOME 之类的系统环境变量复用于临时工作。随后，一条格式错误的清理命令可能会指向实际的主目录，而不是临时文件夹。 - 还有一些情况是，模型试图删除或覆盖某个临时路径，却没有检查那里已经有什么。我们已在多个层面添加了防护措施： - 现在已明确指示 Codex 在执行操作前检查删除目标、创建全新的临时目录、避免复用系统环境变量、优先选择可恢复的操作，并在范围不明确时停止。 - 我们加强了用于识别高风险删除命令并升级审查的执行检查。如果命令被拒绝，模型会被引导采取更安全的方式。 - 我们让 Full access 更难被意外启用，添加了更清晰的警告，并进一步限制了风险特别高的权限组合。 - 我们更新了 Auto-review，以更好地识别破坏性操作。 - 我们构建了有针对性的评估，用于重放我们观察到的故障。我们还在添加针对这些风险的强化学习任务和评分器，并从训练数据中过滤破坏性操作。在这些重放评估中，这些变更大幅减少了该行为，同时保留了 Codex 完成正常编码工作的能力。你这边需要做两件事： - 保持 Codex 应用为最新版本。我们一直在改进安全性、性能以及许多其他方面。 - 使用其中一种沙盒模式：“Ask for approval”或“Approve for me”。只在你信任且可以恢复的环境中使用 Full access。感谢大家，祝 Codex 使用愉快！
viewpoints.originalContent: Hi! Recapping some changes we have rolled out over the last couple of weeks that have further reduced the risk associated to potentially destructive actions being performed by Codex during its work. A few weeks ago, we started investigating a small number of reports where GPT-5.6 in Codex took destructive actions outside what the user asked for. The most serious pattern we found was a command meant to clean up temporary work that could instead delete the user files. This should obviously not happen. Here’s what we found: - Codex sometimes creates temporary folders while working and cleans them up afterward. In rare cases, GPT-5.6 got that cleanup wrong. One pattern involved reusing a system environment variable like $HOME for temporary work. A malformed cleanup command could then point at the actual home directory instead of the temporary folder. - There were cases where the model tried to delete or overwrite a temporary path without checking what was already there. We’ve added protections at several layers: - Codex is now explicitly instructed to check deletion targets before acting, create fresh temporary directories, avoid repurposing system environment variables, prefer recoverable actions, and stop when the scope is unclear. - We strengthened the execution checks that identify high-risk deletion commands and escalate them for review. If a command is rejected, the model is directed to take a safer approach. - We made Full access harder to enable accidentally, added clearer warnings, and further restricted especially risky permission combinations. - We updated Auto-review to better identify destructive actions. - We built targeted evaluations that replay the failures we observed. We’re also adding reinforcement-learning tasks and graders focused on these risks, and filtering destructive actions from training data. In those replay evaluations, the changes substantially reduced the behavior while preserving Codex’s ability to complete normal coding work. Two things to do on your end: - Keep the Codex app up to date. We are always improving safety, performance and many other things. - Use one of the sandbox modes: "Ask for approval" or "Approve for me". Only use…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 正如我们在一个又一个案例研究中所看到的，事实证明，AI模型与最终用户工作流之间能够创造的价值量，远超许多人的假设或认知。模型能力显然在智能体产品中承担了大量重任，但要将AI扩散到企业中，仍有大量工作要做。 1. 让智能体在关键任务工作流中良好运行（并与人类协同），往往需要根据业务流程的不同而采用不同的呈现方式。有时是聊天体验。有时是在确定性工作流中运行的后台智能体。还有数十种其他变体。这既需要针对特定工作领域调优的框架，也需要让它以合适的产品体验呈现出来。 2. 不同的工作流接入完全不同的企业系统，并需要访问截然不同的数据。处理这些数据——无论是生命科学、金融、法律等领域——都需要情境化的方法、对数据的理解、合适的数据交互用户体验，等等。 3. 在大多数垂直领域中，针对特定领域的变革管理需求仍然至关重要。你在银行谈论和实施技术的方式，与律所截然不同。拥有具备单一使命的合适人才，对于流程再造这样复杂的事情来说，最终会极其有用。 4. 能够使用多种模型，意味着你可以将工作流调优到不同的成本和性能水平。而且你最终可以对特定任务进行模型后训练，以定制结果，并挤出前沿模型无法提供的收益。 5. 评估！如果AI无法被评估，它基本上就没有用处。针对特定领域的评估能让你大幅提升框架在特定工作流中的表现，鉴于经济中任务数量之多，这有着极长的长尾效应。几乎不可能有一个系统能为所有任务调优。 6. 许多垂直领域和行业需要定价模型能够反映在纯token之上的相关抽象。能够以符合你所在行业消费模式的方式定价，在多种场景下最终都很重要。 这只是触及了应用AI层所涉及的部分内容。但这一切加起来，构成了一个巨大的可创新和差异化的可持续空间。
viewpoints.originalContent: As we’re seeing in case study after case study, it turns out that the amount of value that can be created between the AI model and the ultimate end-user workflow is far larger than many people assumed or realized. Model capability is obviously doing a lot of heavy lifting in agentic products, but there’s still a lot more work to diffuse AI into the enterprise. 1. Getting agents to work well (and alongside people) in mission critical workflows tends to need to be represented differently depending on the business process. Sometimes it’s a chat experience. Other times it’s a background agent running in a deterministic workflow. And dozens of other variants. This is a mix of needing a harness that’s tuned to specific domains of work, but also making it show up in the right product experience. 2. Different workflows connect into entirely different enterprise systems and need access to very different data. Working with that data -whether it’s life sciences, financial, legal, etc.- requires contextual approaches, understanding of the data, having the right user experience for data interaction, and more. 3. The need for domain-specific change management remains critical in most verticals. The way you talk and implement technology at a bank is very different from a law firm. Having the right talent with a singular mission ends up being extremely useful for something as complex as process reengineering. 4. The ability to work with a variety of models means you can tune the workflows to different cost and performance levels. And you can eventually post train models for specific tasks to tailor the outcomes and eke out gains that aren’t coming otherwise in frontier models. 5. Evals! AI is basically not useful if it can’t be evaluated. Domain-specific evals that let you dramatically improve the performance of your harness for specific workflows just has a crazy long tail given how many tasks there are in the economy. Nearly impossible for one system to be tuned for all of them. 6. Lots of verticals and domains require pricing models that reflect relevant abstractions on top of tokens alone. viewpoints.originalContent: The best way to get good at evals is to take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable. Study the actual traces - the sequence of prompts typical users have, what good responses would look like at each step and for the end to end outcome. Study where your product fails and create traces that capture them - messy tool call responses, missing context etc. Once you have a good eval, think about how you would make it easy to run repeatedly and automatically. Once you have that, think about how you will ensure your eval continues to mirror live traffic as your users patterns evolve. This could be a series. Would you guys like me to write about it everyday?

viewpoints.translatedContent: 以下是如何在 Codex 中为 GPT-5.6 Sol 启用 1M token 上下文窗口的方法。尽管我们已将 Codex 的上下文限制调校为在性能和成本方面达到最优，但这是一个常见需求，因此在此记录说明。更大的上下文窗口可让 Codex 在总结较早内容之前保留更多代码、工具输出和对话历史。你需要一个支持该功能的模型。例如，GPT-5.6 Sol 具有文档记载的 1,050,000 token 窗口。打开 ~/.codex/config.toml，并在任何 [section] 标题之前，于顶层添加或更新以下设置：``` model = "gpt-5.6-sol" model_context_window = 1000000 model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000 ``` 第一项设置用于选择模型。第二项告诉 Codex 使用一百万 token 的上下文预算。第三项在约 900,000 token 时启动自动历史压缩，留出一些余量。保存后重启 Codex 客户端并开始新会话。若要在不更改默认设置的情况下，为单个 CLI 会话尝试此配置：``` codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \ -c model_context_window=1000000 \ -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000 ``` 玩得开心，但也要知道，我们对默认设置进行了精心调校！
viewpoints.originalContent: Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented. A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers: ``` model = "gpt-5.6-sol" model_context_window = 1000000 model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000 ``` The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults: ``` codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \ -c model_context_window=1000000 \ -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000 ``` Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我也对权力集中化的假设持怀疑态度，这一观点源自刘易斯·芒福德1964年的论述：“从近东新石器时代晚期一直到今天，两种技术反复并存：一种是权威主义的，另一种是民主的，前者以系统为中心，力量极其强大，但本质上不稳定，后者以人为中心，相对弱小，却灵活而持久。”这一观点在山谷中引起共鸣。彼得·蒂尔在2018年曾说：“加密货币是自由意志主义的，而人工智能是共产主义的。”当然，如今看来，人工智能似乎正朝着更加集中化的方向发展。如果你是一个坚定的AGI信徒，你会相信这一趋势将持续下去。但我们也看到针对特定用途的微调模型正在复苏。正如阿姆贾德所说，人类大脑为去中心化的好处提供了非常有力的证据。我们可能只是还没看到这一点，因为人工智能仍处于高度文字化的“蜜蜂”或“蚂蚁”时代。如果最优设计继续是最大程度集中化的，我会感到惊讶。
viewpoints.originalContent: i am also skeptical of the centralization of power hypothesis it comes from Lewis Mumford in 1964 who argued: "from late Neolithic times in the Near East, right down to our own day, two technologies have recurrently existed side by side: one authoritarian, the other democratic, the first system-centered, immensely powerful, but inherently unstable, the other man-centered, relatively weak, but resourceful and durable." this echoes around the valley. peter thiel said in 2018, "crypto is libertarian and AI is communist" certainly today, it seems like we're on track for AI to look more centralized. if you are a hardcore AGI person you believe this will continue. but we're also seeing a resurgence of fine tuning models for specific purposes. and as amjad says, the human brain provides very good evidence for the benefits of decentralization. we just may not see it yet because we're still in the hyperliterate "bee" or "ant" days of AI i'd be surprised if the optimal design continues to be maximally centralized

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于AI智能体的价值以及机遇所在，这是一个相当不错的思考方式。你拥有一种技术，它会不知疲倦地完成你以前永远无法完全做到的所有事情。不是因为你不想做，也不是因为那些事没有价值，而是因为这在过去甚至根本不具备现实可行性。AI带来的上行空间在于，去思考你现在可以把智能投入到哪些不会放弃的事情上，以及回报会是什么。你不可能找出代码库中的每一个安全漏洞，因为你无法模拟每一种风险向量。你不可能阅读每一份合同或文件来处理数据并加以捕获，以便日后查询。你不可能梳理整个客户群，找出每一个与追加销售相关的数据点。诸如此类。这是一种相当清晰的思路，既能用来思考如何部署AI以获得实际收益，也能用来判断创业机会在哪里。去瞄准那些市场——在这些市场中，对某个问题投入更多算力，将从根本上改变客户在该领域现在能够做到的事情。
viewpoints.originalContent: Pretty good way to think about the value of AI agents and where the opportunity lies. You have a technology that will tirelessly do all the things that you could never fully do before. Not because you didn’t want to or it wasn’t valuable, but because it was just not even remotely practical. The upside with AI is to think about everything you can now throw intelligence at that won’t give up and what would the returns be. You just couldn’t possibly find every security vulnerability in your codebase, because you couldn’t simulate every risk vector. You couldn’t read every contract or document to process the data and capture it to query later. You couldn’t comb through your customer base and look for every relevant data point for doing upsells. And so on. This is a pretty clear way to think about how to deploy AI to get real gains, but also where the startup opportunities are as well. Go after the markets where more compute on a problem will qualitatively change what customers can now do in that domain.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于 token 和每个 token 的价格。我说过会多写一点，所以现在开始：OpenAI 的 token 不等于另一个模型的 token。我们习惯用“每百万 token 多少美元”来比较 AI 价格，好像 token 是一个标准化单位，就像克或千瓦时一样。但它不是。不同模型在处理和生成完全相同的文本时，使用的 token 数量并不相同，这意味着每个 token 的价格更低，并不一定代表最终账单更低。想象两个完全相同的披萨。一个切成 8 片，每片 $2。另一个切成 16 片，每片 $1.25。第二家宣传的每片价格更便宜，但整个披萨要 $20，而不是 $16。真扫兴……你的胃其实并不在乎你刚才吃了多少片。我知道你现在饿了，但回到 token。在一次涵盖英语、技术、多语言和数字文本的小范围比较中，我们用于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的分词器使用了 766 个 token，而 Claude Opus 5 估计使用了 1,170 个。这是一个非常显著的差异，大约少了 34.5% 的 token。你可以得到完全相同的文本，却要为所有那些额外的 token 付费。每个 token 的价格并不能真正说明这个问题。即使修正了分词器差异，也还是没抓住更关键的一点。真正重要的是每个成功结果的价格，而要做到这一点，你可以把基准测试当作起点，但最终必须在自己的使用场景中实际尝试和衡量。就这些。愿 token 流动不息。
viewpoints.originalContent: On tokens and prices per token. I said I’d write more about this, so here goes: an OpenAI token != another model’s token. We compare AI prices in dollars per million tokens as if a token were a standardized unit, like a gram or a kilowatt-hour. It isn’t. Different models use and produce the exact same text using different numbers of tokens, which means a lower price per token does not necessarily mean a lower bill. Imagine two identical pizzas. One is cut into 8 slices at $2 each. The other is cut into 16 slices at $1.25 each. The second place advertises cheaper slices, but the whole pizza costs $20 instead of $16. Bummer ... your stomach doesn't actually care about the number of slices you just ate. I know you are hungry now, but back to tokens. In one small comparison spanning English, technical, multilingual, and numerical text, the tokenizer we use for GPT-5.6 Sol used 766 tokens versus an estimated 1,170 for Claude Opus 5. That's a very significant difference of about 34.5% fewer tokens. You can get the same exact text, but pay for all those extra tokens. The price per token doesn't really tell this story. Even correcting for tokenizer differences misses the bigger point. What actually matters is price per successful outcome, and for that you can use benchmarks as a starting point, but really you have to try it and measure on your own use cases. That's all. May the tokens flow.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 令人惊叹的成果。Cursor 完美地执行了应用型 AI 战略。大多数人完全低估了 AI 编程的市场规模。历史上最大的开发者工具退出案例，规模也不过是数十亿美元级别。而且当他们真正起步时，这个领域已经被认为是竞争激烈且有些饱和的空间。多个思维模型几乎瞬间被打破。智能体编程的市场规模远比大多数人意识到的要大得多。在用户与底层模型之间，甚至在模型本身之上，实际上还有大量大量的创新空间。Cursor 提供了应用型 AI 的实战手册：为智能体编程工作找到正确的产品形态，在模型与工作流之间充当中立层，对最有意义的领域进行模型后训练以降低成本或提升性能，为相关工作流构建合适的基础设施栈，打造与品类高度契合的市场推广动作，等等。对于当下任何从事应用型 AI 的人来说，这是一组极好的经验教训。我们将会看到更多这样的案例。
viewpoints.originalContent: Amazing outcome. Cursor executed the applied AI strategy flawlessly. Most people completely underestimated the market size in AI coding. The biggest developer tool exits in history were on the order of low billions of dollars. And it was already assumed to be a heavily competitive and somewhat saturated space when they really got going. Multiple mental models shattered near instantly. The market sizes for agentic coding was far larger than most realized. There was actually tons and tons of room to innovate between the user and the underlying model, and even on the model itself. Cursor provided out the applied AI playbook by figuring out the right product shape for agentic coding work, acting as a neutral layer between models and the workflows, post training models for the areas that make most sense to drive down costs or improve performance, building out the right infra stack for the relevant workflows, building out a strong category-aligned GTM motion, and more. Great set of lessons for anyone doing applied AI right now. We’re going to see a lot more of these.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 提高蒸汽机效率增加了煤炭需求。高级语言让编程更简单，结果构建了远更多的软件。电子表格降低了财务分析成本，导致企业进行远更多的分析。当一项任务的成本和复杂性下降时，新的应用场景在经济上变得可行。人工智能加软件工程很可能会遵循同样的模式：远更多的软件解决远更多的问题，包括那些以前在经济上不可行的问题。
viewpoints.originalContent: Making steam engines more efficient increased coal demand. Higher-level languages made programming easier and resulted in far more software being built. Spreadsheets made financial analysis cheaper and resulted in businesses doing far more analysis. When the cost and complexity of a task falls, new use cases become economically viable. AI + software engineering will likely follow the same pattern: far more software solving far more problems, including problems that were previously economically unviable.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于工程师将被淘汰的说法，是当时流传的较为疯狂的假设之一。简直错得离谱。我们只是给了工程师一件可以加速开发任何我们想要之物的强力工具。当然，在那个世界里，他们的价值不仅依然至关重要，而且在许多领域实际上还会上升，因为我们可以将工程应用于比以前多得多的工作。如果你试图自动化药物发现，你需要工程师。如果你试图自动化制造业，你需要工程师。如果你承接越来越大的软件项目，你需要工程师。这种情况也会发生在工程以外的领域。人工智能促使公司承担比以前多得多的工作，这导致需要更多专家来监督这些工作。即使模型变得越来越好，这些领域的专家也能比新手更好地利用它们。现在正是成为专家的好时代。
viewpoints.originalContent: The elimination of engineers was one of the wilder hypotheses out there. Just like absurdly wrong. We just gave engineers a power tool that can accelerate the development of whatever we want. Of course their value not only remains critical in that world, but actually goes up in many domains because we can apply engineering to far more work than before. If you’re trying to automate drug discovery, you need engineers. If you’re trying to automate manufacturing, you need engineers. If you’re taking on larger and larger software projects, you need engineers. This will happen in domains beyond engineering too. AI causes companies to take on way more work than before, which leads to needing more experts to oversee the work. Even as models get better and better, they can be better utilized by the experts in those fields than the novices. Great time to be an expert.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我很好奇X是如何对抗AI垃圾内容的，于是去看了它的开源算法。它有一个名为TweetSpamBot的行为模型，会分析最多512条近期账户操作，观察诸如发帖爆发、引用转发行为、时间规律，以及操作之间的正常浏览或停留等信号。该模型经过训练，能够识别以下模式：→ TWEET_CREATE_BURST → QUOTE_TWEET_SPAMMER → CONTENT_AMPLIFIER 在上述方面得分高，可能会触发账户验证，但似乎并不会降低这些垃圾帖子本身的排序。我认为这里的缺口在于，该模型并不读取实际的帖子内容。因此，一个精密的AI内容工厂仍然可以整天发布垃圾内容：1. 找到爆款帖子 2. 每次都套用同一个模板进行引用转发：钩子 → 数据 → 背景故事 → 要点 3. 每天在毫不相关的话题上重复10次以上 如果@X不想变得像LinkedIn那样，我认为它应该考虑关注那些反复将不相关的爆款帖子，以高频率转化为同一模板引用转发垃圾内容的账户。目前上述防护措施太容易被绕过了。
viewpoints.originalContent: I was curious how X is fighting AI slop, so I looked at its open-source algorithm. It has a behavioral model called TweetSpamBot that analyzes up to 512 recent account actions, looking at signals like posting bursts, quote-post behavior, timing, and normal browsing or dwell between actions. The model is trained to recognize patterns such as: → TWEET_CREATE_BURST → QUOTE_TWEET_SPAMMER → CONTENT_AMPLIFIER A high score on the above can feed into an account challenge but doesn't seem to downrank the slop posts themselves. I think the gap here is that the model doesn’t read the actual post content. So a sophisticated AI content mill can still post slop all day long: 1. Find viral posts 2. Quote tweet with the same template each time: hook → numbers → backstory → takeaway 3. Repeat 10+ times a day across unrelated topics If @X doesn't want to become like LinkedIn, I think it should consider looking at accounts that repeatedly turn unrelated viral posts into the same templated quote tweet slop at high volume. Right now the guardrails above are too easy to bypass.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Grok Bot 是一次出色的发布……用户体验、设计、引导流程：堪称完美 :chefs-kiss: 但我经常在这两者之间反复纠结：用户（个人和企业）会想要一个掌握所有上下文的超级代理，还是想要被指定去完成一部分任务的子代理？如果我们把代理当作人来对待，那么 Grok Bot 的设计就非常合理。它让我们能够为那个人的部门划分工具、上下文和结果。你带着心中特定的目标去找那个机器人。但是，如果你把代理当作 Jarvis，你就会想要一个能把事情办成的主代理。它可能会创建并协调完成任务所需的所有机器人（甚至包括沟通/上下文）。但界面是 1 对 1，而不是 1 对多。我的猜测是，随着时间推移，它会倾向于一个主代理，这个主代理随后可以充当编排者，读取/理解你创建的机器人。但就像现在大多数公司所做的那样，起步会很窄。附言：我理解核心工程上的限制（上下文窗口、工具使用、简单性、成本等），这也是为什么公司现在选择任务/单一结果。我主要是从设计/产品角度来思考这个问题。
viewpoints.originalContent: Grok Bot is a fantastic release.. the UX, the design, the onboarding :chefs-kiss: But I go back and forth on this a lot: Will users (personal and business) want one super agent that holds all the context or sub agents that are designated to do a slice of tasks? If we treat agents as humans, then the Grok Bot design makes a ton of sense. It allows us to compartmentalize tools, context, outcomes for that person’s division. You reach out to that bot for that specific goal that you have in mind. But, if you treat agents as Jarvis, you want a master agent that just gets the job done. It might create and coordinate all the bots (and dare I say the communication/context) that might be needed to do the task. But the interface is 1:1 vs. 1:many. My guess is it’ll veer towards the one master agent over time who can then act as an orchestrator who reads / understands the bots you create. But starts narrow as most of the companies are doing it now. PS: I understand the core engineering constraints (context windows, tool use, simplicity, cost etc) why companies are choosing task/singular outcomes today. Primarily thinking this from a design / product side.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 从Deepseek和Grok发布新模型的角度来看，今天真是精彩的一天。这两次新模型更新都以极低的成本带来了能力上的巨大飞跃。这真正体现了AI领域的杰文斯悖论正在上演。通过降低AI的成本，需求将继续加速增长。当我与企业交流时，他们希望智能体处理的应用场景，远比他们目前预算所能覆盖的要多得多。他们希望智能体扫描代码库以查找安全问题。他们希望智能体审阅所有文档。他们希望智能体在很大一部分工作流程中处理信息。诸如此类。当我们降低AI的成本或提升能力水平时，就会在企业中开启全新的应用场景，从而推动更大的需求。这对应用AI层也非常有利。模型的选择越多——尤其是那些针对不同类型（或成本）工作调优的模型——处于能够根据任务进行路由和优化的那一层，其价值就越大。目前这对整个技术栈来说都是好事。
viewpoints.originalContent: Awesome day in terms of new model releases from both Deepseek and Grok. Both of these new model updates represent huge jumps in capability at insanely low costs. This is truly Jevons paradox for AI playing out. By bringing down the cost of AI, demand will continue to accelerate. When I talk to enterprises, they have vastly more use-cases for what they’d like agents to handle than generally what they’re able to budget for today. They want agents to scan their codebases for security issues. They want agents to review all their documents. They want agents to process information in a large portion of their workflows. And so on. When we bring down the cost of AI or drive up capability levels, it opens up all new use cases in the enterprises, which drives even greater demand. This is also great for the applied AI layer. The more choice of models - especially those tuned for different types (or costs) of work - the more value there is in being at the layer that can route and optimize based on the task. Great for the entire stack right now.

viewpoints.originalContent: story time.. in 2023 (my previous role) I remember the first time some customers volunteered their prompt logs to us. We were surprised by the number of “build me an app for X” prompts. felt wildly ambitious at the time. models were barely graduating from code completion to generating a useful block of code. But it was a great signal of what people actually wanted, and shaped a lot of our vision: systems that could design, build and deploy an app end to end from a simple ask. Pretty wild that 3 yrs later we’re basically there.

viewpoints.originalContent: LLMs still produce bugs, but those bugs are different than what they used to be. It’s less off-by-ones and more about system design, ui usability, missing broader context. Some kinds of coding has been solved, but not all. While models continue to improve, adversarial code review has been an incredibly powerful tool to catch many of these kinds of bugs. It can be as simple as a one line prompt - “use a dynamic workflow to adversarial test every edge case in an iOS simulator”, or use Claude’s built in /code-review (or /code-review low, /code-review medium, etc.)

viewpoints.translatedContent: 关于如何思考FDE的好文章。关键在于，FDE是真实存在的，而且在可预见的未来不会从AI领域消失。之所以现在出现前所未有的规模，是因为AI本质上是在将非确定性、快速变化的系统引入此前大多从未被自动化的流程中。这与实施传统软件看起来几乎完全不同。 “如果你在2026年为会计工作构建一个AI智能体，并不存在既定的工作流程，因为实际上从来没有人使用过这类东西。没有人知道用户旅程是什么样的——你不知道，更重要的是，你的客户也不知道。他们无法告诉你他们想要什么，因为他们想要的那个东西还没有成形。” 软件在很大程度上一直是确定性的，一旦有效实施，对客户来说运行方式始终相同。这意味着前期的实施工作在相似客户之间是*相对*统一的，而且系统通常不会以根本性方式频繁升级。AI智能体几乎在每一个维度上都完全不同。客户的业务流程必须改变才能与智能体协同工作，要让智能体在客户的最终状态流程中正常运行，需要大量——且必要的——定制化工作，评估需要持续运行，AI模型在不断变化，更新需要不断被纳入，底层框架和更广泛的系统往往也会因客户反馈而改变，还有很多其他方面。这对客户、系统集成商和应用型AI供应商来说都是实实在在的工作。即使AI能力大幅提升，这项工作依然存在（甚至变得更加复杂），因为企业只会把越来越复杂的流程交给智能体。现在正是成为FDE的好时机。
viewpoints.originalContent: Good post on how to think about FDEs. The key is that FDEs are real and not going away for AI any time soon. The reason this is happening now at a scale that has never been seen before is because AI is fundamentally about adding a non-deterministic, rapidly changing system to workflows that largely have never been automated before. This looks very little like implementing traditional software. “If you're building an AI agent for accounting in 2026, there is no established workflow, because literally nobody has ever used one of these. Nobody knows what the user journey looks like — not you, and importantly, not your customer either. They can't tell you what they want, because the thing they'd want doesn't have a shape yet.” Software has largely always been deterministic and once implemented effectively worked the same for customers. This meant the upfront implementation work was *relatively* uniform across similar customers, and the system wasn’t regularly being upgraded in fundamental ways. AI agents are entirely different on nearly every dimension. The customer’s business process has to change to work with agents, there is heavy -necessary- customization to get agents to work in the customers end-state process, evals need to be run constantly, the AI models are constantly changing and updates need to keep getting incorporated, the underlying harness and broader system are often changing due to customer feedback, and much more. This is real work for the customer, systems integrators, and the applied AI vendors. Even as AI capabilities improve dramatically, this work remains (or even gets more complicated) given enterprises will just throw increasingly more complex processes at agents. Great time to be an FDE.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 最近我深陷于AI与消费者体验交叉领域的探索：如何构建一套理论来解释用户行为背后的动机，而非仅仅记录其行为轨迹？消费类产品既包含搜索/聊天产生的显性信号，也包含观看、跳过、停留、回访等行为留下的隐性信号。要真正理解这些信号的含义，需要结合情境进行推理——用户生活中正在发生什么，外部世界正在发生什么，以及他们的兴趣如何随时间演变。而要在近实时状态下为数十亿用户规模的消费体验实现这一点，则是完全不同的挑战。
viewpoints.originalContent: been deep down this rabbit hole at the intersection of AI and consumer experiences recently: How do you develop a theory of why someone did something, rather than just a history of what they did? Consumer products have a mix of explicit signals from search/chat and implicit signals from what you watch, skip, linger on, revisit. understanding what those signals actually mean requires reasoning about context - what’s happening in someone’s life, what’s happening in the world, and how their interests are evolving over time. and doing this in a near real-time manner for billion user consumer experiences is a whole other challenge.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Vercel Sandbox 同时隔离了 ① 计算环境与 ② 网络环境。Kimi 的论文表明，基于容器的隔离对于前沿模型而言并不足够。Vercel Sandbox 采用强力的微虚拟机隔离来应对 ① 计算隔离问题。OpenAI 的逃逸事件则发生在通往 Artifactory 的 ② 网络路径上。我们的出站防火墙现已免费开放，以便大家进一步约束行为异常的智能体的网络活动。¹ “在我们早期使用传统容器沙箱运行环境的实验中，我们观察到多次由非预期的智能体操作引发的内核崩溃与死锁。” 🔗 github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/master/k3_tech_report.pdf ² “为了获取互联网访问权限，这些模型识别并利用了 Artifactory（一个软件包注册表缓存代理）中一个此前未知的零日漏洞” 🔗 openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/
viewpoints.originalContent: Vercel Sandbox isolates both ① compute and ② network. Kimi's paper shows container-based isolation is not enough for frontier models. Vercel Sandbox uses strong microVM isolation to address ①. OpenAI's escape was on ② the network path to Artifactory. Our egress firewall is now free so everyone can constrain misbehaving agents' network activity further. ¹ "in our early experiments with traditional container-based sandbox runtimes, we observed several kernel panics and deadlocks caused by unintended agent operations." 🔗 github⁠.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/master/k3_tech_report.pdf ² "to gain Internet access, the models identified and exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in Artifactory⁠, a package registry cache proxy" 🔗 openai⁠.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/

viewpoints.translatedContent: 企业内不同工作流程对持续、不间断计算机工作的契合度各异，这是导致智能体扩散速度不均的原因之一。智能编码之所以呈现爆发式增长，关键在于这类工作的经济价值与纯数字信息产出直接挂钩，且单次任务量理论上可无限扩展。这意味着随着AI智能体单次处理能力提升，以及模型在该任务类型上的能力增强，它们几乎能即时部署到更大规模的工作负载中。但当前多数工作流程的设计并不天然具备这种特性。销售代表需要与客户建立反馈循环才能推进特定客户的工作，律师需要与委托人沟通，医生需要与患者互动。因此，大规模的智能体工作至少在默认形态上，很可能不会与编码领域雷同。相反，在许多这类领域中，智能体需要融入为AI重新设计的工作流程。Factory公司的马坦·格林伯格在《训练数据》播客中提出了精辟见解：如果明天所有人都请病假，令牌使用量将骤降，因为无人发出指令。这揭示了当前智能体在后台自主运行的程度之低，而未来这恰恰应成为智能体工作的主流形态。在法律领域，它将处理每份流入的合同；在销售领域，智能体将遍历客户记录，识别最佳外联时机；在生命科学研究中，将是智能体集群研读每项测试或全部研究成果。要实现这些，业务流程必须重构以支持智能体，而非延续当前大量依赖人工的模式。这正是当下的重大机遇，但其扩散方式将与智能编码截然不同——涉及大量变革管理、数据清理、流程再造等工作。
viewpoints.originalContent: One reason why we’re going to get uneven diffusion rates of agents is because different workflows in the enterprise are more or less aligned to continuous, uninterrupted computer work. A big reason why agentic coding growth has gone completely vertical is because it’s a type of work where economic value is directly correlated with the output of solely digital information, and where the task size can in theory be unbounded in a single session. This means that as AI agents can do larger amounts of work at a time, and as model capability improves on this task type, they can directly be deployed at larger workloads near instantaneously. Lots of work doesn’t natively have this property in how today’s workflows are designed. A sales rep needs a feedback loop with the customer before they can do additional work for a specific account, a lawyer needs to talk to the client, and a doctor needs to interact with a patient. So large agentic work will likely not look the same as it has in coding, at least by default. Instead, in many of these domains, the agents will actually need to tie into a workflow that is reengineered for AI. Matan Grinberg at Factory had a good way of thinking about this on the Training Data podcast: if everyone called in sick tomorrow, token usage would plummet because no one would be there to prompt them. This shows how early we are in agents running in the background for most processes; whereas this should be the majority of volume of agentic work in the future. In legal, it will be about processing every contract that comes in, in sales it will be agents that roam through customer records and figure out signals of when to better do outreach, in life sciences research it will be about swarms of agents reading through every test or all research. To do that these business processes have to be wired up to support agents, as opposed to the vast amounts of manual work that we do today. This is the big opportunity right now, but it’s going to diffuse differently from something like agentic coding. Lots of change management, lots of data cleanup, lots of workflow reengineering, and more.

viewpoints.originalContent: Meta releasing Muse Spark 1.2 as open weights is a *very* big deal. America now finally has its response to the open weights AI race. This will continue to help drive down the cost of intelligence, it allows companies to run models as they see fit, as well as allows them to post train their own models for specific use-cases to get better performance gains in their domain. And provides a realistic option for those previously closed off from OSS models. This is broadly net positive for AI - even frontier closed models - because it helps drive further diffusion of AI. Big moment in the AI race.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我不太理解，科技行业为何对数据中心引发的抵触情绪如此不解。 * AI主要由沿海/科技精英打造，他们大多不住在数据中心附近；而住在数据中心附近的人并不信任他们 * 技术工种的需求固然受欢迎，但这仅限于建设期间的短短几年 * 社区不希望AI泡沫破裂后，被半途而废的巨型空置仓库困住 * 他们在日常生活中并未觉得AI有多大帮助 * 没错，数据中心的水资源是闭环循环利用，但电力方面的担忧是真实存在的，能源生产确实会产生影响 诚然，其中有些“邻避效应”，但这些担忧并非全无道理吧？ 我显然是深度支持AI的，但轻视这些担忧，或认为它们是某种中国心理战的产物，感觉又是科技行业一次脱离现实的反应。 我们需要做得更好。
viewpoints.originalContent: I don't understand what the tech industry doesn't understand about resistance against data centers. * AI is mostly built by coastal/tech elites who generally don't live near data centers; people near data centers don't trust them * Trade jobs demand is welcome, but it's just for a few years during construction * Communities don't want to be stuck with half-finished gigantic empty warehouses if the AI bubble bursts; * they don't find AI particularly helpful in their daily lives. * yes data centers run in close loops for water but elecriticy concerns are real and energy generation does have an impact Yes some NIMBYism but those concerns are not entirely unreasonable? I'm obviously deeply pro-AI but dismissing concerns or thinking they're the result of some Chinese psyOps feels like another tone-deaf moment for the tech industry. We need to do better.
viewpoints.role: VC at FirstMarkCap. Host: MAD Podcast; Organizer: Data Driven NYC, Author: MAD Landscape.

viewpoints.title: 大型科技公司难以构建AI产品的一个原因在于，它们的组织结构是为之前的软件范式设计的。层层叠叠、等级森严、规避风险、渐进式思维，以及被评审拖垮。基于智能模型进行构建是一门不同的技艺。一些旧有的直觉可以沿用，但有些则需要摒弃。然而，太多公司不愿下功夫脱去旧壳。
viewpoints.translatedContent: 大型科技公司难以构建AI产品的一个原因在于，它们的组织结构是为之前的软件范式设计的。层层叠叠、等级森严、规避风险、渐进式思维，以及被评审拖垮。基于智能模型进行构建是一门不同的技艺。一些旧有的直觉可以沿用，但有些则需要摒弃。然而，太多公司不愿下功夫脱去旧壳。
viewpoints.originalContent: One reason big tech is struggling to build AI products is their orgs were designed for the previous software paradigm. Layered, hierarchical, risk averse, incremental thinking, death by reviews. Building on intelligent models is a different craft. Some of the old instincts transfer. Some need to be unlearned. Too many refuse to do the hard work of shedding their old skin.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 无论您是在企业内推动AI应用，还是为企业打造AI解决方案，这篇帖子都极具价值。AI带来的生产力提升幅度将大相径庭——远超您的想象——因为如果您从根本上改变工作流程以支持智能代理，在前沿领域所能实现的成果将极为显著。挑战在于，大多数人不会或无法自然而然地做到这一点，因为这涉及到的复杂性太高。因此，大量基于智能代理的自动化将来自于将代理无缝接入工作流程，而用户最终甚至不会察觉或在意：“对于其他人来说，工作必须在不改变他们工作方式的前提下完成，这意味着AI要退居幕后。为什么AI非得由人来提示呢？只需找出最重复的流程，在员工已习惯的现有记录系统中构建代理即可。” 对于当下大多数希望从AI中获得显著收益的企业来说，这才是真正需要着手的工作。少一些“百花齐放”的思路，多一些“找出企业中10个杠杆效应最高的环节，并对其应用自动化”的做法。这里没有真正的捷径可走。
viewpoints.originalContent: Great post both if you’re driving AI in an enterprise or building for an enterprise. AI productivity gains are going to wildly vary - much wider than you think - because what you can do at the frontier is so significant if you fundamentally change your workflows to support agents. The challenge is that most people won’t or can’t naturally do this because of the complexity it entails. Thus, a large amount of automation with agents is going to come from just getting agents wired up into a workflow that the user never ends up noticing or caring about: “For everybody else, the work has to get done without them changing how they work, which means the AI goes into the background. Why do you need AI to be prompted by a human anyway? Just figure out what the most repetitive processes are, build agents in your existing systems of record that employees are used to” This is the real work ahead for most enterprises right now that want to get significant gains from AI. A lot less “let a thousand flowers bloom” and more “pick off the 10 highest leverage things in the enterprise and apply automation to them”. There’s no real shortcut here.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 观点正确。全球99%的算力消耗将发生在企业场景中。这些算力将用于编写代码、梳理海量生命科学研究数据、实现制造自动化、保障企业安全、检测欺诈行为，以及成千上万类似具有重大经济价值的任务。这既是AI成本最能被合理化的领域，也是并行工作者代你执行任务最能发挥效用的地方。即便是对消费者影响最大的智能体，也往往会被包装成端到端服务——消费者根本不会意识到另一端存在AI系统，比如更快捷的保险理赔或银行开户流程。关键在于，智能体在经济各领域的渗透需要数年时间，因为必须重新设计工作流程以融入AI，这将彻底改变当前大多数工作的运作方式。任何期待一夜之间实现变革的人，都应该调整自己的时间预期。
viewpoints.originalContent: Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful. Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank. The key though is it’s going to take years for diffusion of agents across the economy because workflows have to re-engineered to incorporate AI, which is a complete change to how most work happens today. Anyone who’s expecting this to happen overnight should be updating their timelines.

viewpoints.originalContent: .@TryRivo is building self-driving finance. Agents connect to the checking account you already have, learn your cash flow, sweep dollars into Treasury-backed yield, and bring them back before your bills hit. Every dollar earns until the moment you spend it. Why is this hard? Prediction under asymmetric cost. Money returned a day early costs you a little yield. Money returned a day late bounces a bill and destroys trust. @AmbrishTweets is one of the few people who has shipped this class of system before. PhD in AI, 7,000+ citations, built consumer AI at Amazon, and led the L4 autonomy work at Cruise that launched robotaxis, before he came through @spc as a Founder Fellow. Self-driving cars took two decades because the last edge cases were the hard ones. Self-driving money is the same problem with a friendlier failure mode, and the founder building it has already solved the harder version once.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 与众多企业深度交流的一大乐趣在于，你能亲眼看到当前公司中存在的各种AI实施策略。与云计算的早期阶段不同——当时只有少数几种部署模式，且受限于仅有的几家基础设施供应商——AI在企业中的落地方式实际上要丰富得多。如果你问10位IT负责人他们的编码代理策略是什么，你至少会得到5种不同的答案。如果询问他们的终端用户生产力代理，有些企业已标准化使用ChatGPT或Claude，有些则提供多种解决方案供选择，还有许多企业构建了自己的编排层，让员工可以使用任何模型。就模型而言，我们知道那些主流大模型，但企业正越来越多地尝试开源模型，或者至少对开源模型充满好奇，一旦有合适且感觉安全的产品出现，就会立即采用。此外，越来越多的垂直领域模型和代理也在企业中涌现，用于各种定制化用例。在数据访问方面，有些企业直接让代理扮演用户角色，而另一些则设置拥有独立身份的代理用户。有些公司正在为代理的行为设置大量护栏，而其他公司则将责任交给用户。鉴于早期阶段就已呈现如此多样性，这意味着我们将迎来多年的格局变化。任何已经预测最终市场结果的人，很可能都会出错，因为一切尚未正式定型。前方机遇广阔。
viewpoints.originalContent: One fun benefit of spending so much time with enterprises is you get to see the array of AI implementation strategies that exist in companies right now. Unlike the early innings of cloud where there were really only a couple deployment patterns available -including being limited by only a couple infra vendors existing- AI actually has a much wider range of approaches in the enterprise. If you ask 10 IT leaders what their coding agent strategy looks like, you get at least 5 different answers. If you ask about their end-user productivity agents, some have standardized on ChatGPT or Claude, others offer a choice of multiple solutions, and many have built their own orchestration layers for employees to use any model. For models, we know the big ones, but increasingly enterprises are experimenting with OSS models, or are at least immensely curious about OSS and would jump at the right offering that felt safe. And increasingly there’s a set of vertical models and agents that equally show up in enterprises for a range of tailored use-cases. For accessing data, some enterprises just have agents take on the role of the user, and others are setting up agent users that have their own identities. Some companies are setting up substantial guardrails on what agents can do, and others are putting responsibility on the user. Given this heterogeneity this early on at the start, it means we’re in for years of landscape changes. Anyone who’s predicting ultimate market outcomes already probably will be wrong as nothing has formally settled in yet. Lots of opportunity ahead.

viewpoints.originalContent: The best model for early product validation is almost never the best model for production. Talked to a bunch of founders this weekend. There’s a standard playbook emerging : 1/ Prototype with the best frontier models. Max quality. Ignore cost and latency. Learn what users actually want and iterate. 2/ Once the workflow and UX is validated, optimize like crazy for cost and latency - prompt eng, model routing, harnesses, smaller models, fine tuning. I see most teams get stuck in step 1.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Next.js 16.3：更快、更好、更强。我的亮点：0️⃣ 更快的开发与构建速度 感谢 Fable 改进了内存使用，以及团队实现了增量 𝚗𝚎𝚡𝚝 𝚋𝚞𝚒𝚕𝚍 缓存。1️⃣ 即时导航体验 🔥 用户想要单页应用，他们就该得到单页应用。开启即时导航（很快将成为默认设置）后，你的智能体基本上就被迫让一切变快。2️⃣ 面向智能体的开发体验 如果你愿意，仍然可以保留“慢速”导航，比如像 PHP 老式做法那样，在服务端数据获取时阻塞导航。但即便如此，你的智能体也会获得*选择权*，例如设置 <𝚂𝚞𝚜𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚜𝚎 𝚏𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚋𝚊𝚌𝚔> 来实现即时加载骨架。智能体还能获得内置的版本化文档。这是迄今为止我们为智能体打造的最佳版本，也会让你的升级过程非常顺畅。我轻松地将自己的项目升级到了 16.3 并启用了即时导航，让我的智能体毫无问题地完成了所有迁移工作。还有更多亮点。16.3 在服务成本上更高效，无论是自托管还是无服务器环境。类型检查也更快……感谢本次发布的 90 位贡献者！
viewpoints.originalContent: Next.js 16.3: faster, better, stronger. My highlights: 0️⃣ Faster dev & builds Shoutout to Fable for improving memory use, and the team for landing the incremental 𝚗𝚎𝚡𝚝 𝚋𝚞𝚒𝚕𝚍 cache. 1️⃣ Instant navigations are 🔥 The people wanted SPAs, they shall get SPAs. By turning on instant navs (which will soon be default), your agent is basically forced to make things fast. 2️⃣ Agent-native DX You can still ship "slow" navs if you want, e.g. by blocking navs on server-side data fetching ala PHP olden days. But even then, your agent will be given *choices*, like setting up a <𝚂𝚞𝚜𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚜𝚎 𝚏𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚋𝚊𝚌𝚔> for instant loading shells. Agents also get built-in versioned docs. This is our best release for agents by far, which will also make your upgrading journey very smooth. I've had an easy time bumping my projects to 16.3 and enabling instant navs, having my agent migrate everything without issues. And so much more. 16.3 is more cost-efficient to serve, both in self-hosting and serverless environments. Faster to type-check… Thank you to the 90 contributors to this release!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 我们将看到，AI在个人生活和日常生产力中的应用，与其在数学、科学、法律、编程等深度领域的能力之间，差距会越来越大。在达到某个阈值之前，所有领域都能均匀感受到AI的能力提升，因为模型总体上只是变得稍微有用了一些。而现在，深度领域的工作即将迎来垂直突破。大多数人不会在日常生活中直接注意到这些好处（当然，随着时间的推移，他们会间接感受到），但这些领域的专家会。与消费者领域需求相对容易满足不同，深度领域所需的能力没有固有的上限。不过，这往往会导致能力过剩，因为许多性能提升需要以应用的方式融入特定工作领域的数据集和工作流程中。但最终，这正是生命科学、现实世界自动化、新型网络能力等领域取得突破的方式。
viewpoints.originalContent: We’re going to see an increasing divergence between what AI does in our personal lives and in daily productivity vs. what it can do in very deep domains like math, science, legal, coding and more. Up to some threshold, capability was evenly felt across all domains because the models were just becoming mildly useful in general. Now, the deep domain work is about to go vertical. Most people won’t actually notice these benefits in their day to day life directly (indirectly they certainly will over time), but the experts in these fields will. And there’s no inherent ceiling to what capabilities are needed, unlike in the consumer space where needs can get met relatively straightforwardly. This will often lead to a capability overhang, though, as many of these performance gains need to be applied to data sets and workflows in an applied way for that area of work. But this is ultimately how you get breakthroughs in life sciences, real world automation, new cyber capabilities, and more.

viewpoints.originalContent: No idea if these specific numbers generalize across tasks, but directionally it’s clear that the harness is going to become the most important variable -right next to model capability- in the AI stack. The ability for harnesses to break down work in the most efficient way and route to the right model at the right time is going to be a huge variable for maximizing accuracy and reducing costs. We’re actually still incredibly early in this journey. The harness didn’t matter that much when tasks only took hundreds of thousands or millions of tokens. But as we have tasks that take tens of millions and hundreds of millions of tokens, this becomes a major variable. Huge opportunity ahead.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Linear 中最常见的循环是这种变体（问题 > 代理 > PR > 发布），大约 30% 的缺陷会完整走完这个流程。但实际操作中有一些细微之处——指令应要求代理深入调查问题的根本原因，并使用 Datadog 和 Sentry MCP 收集更多证据。只有在高度确定的情况下才应尝试提供修复方案，否则会消耗大量 token。如果在研究过程中认为更多证据会有帮助，比如请报告者提供复现步骤等，代理应在问题上留言请求。代理也需要被教导遵循良好实践，就像人一样！
viewpoints.originalContent: The most common loop written in Linear is some variant this one (Issue > Agent > PR > Release) ~30% of our bugs make it all the way through this flow. But there are some nuances to doing it -- The instructions should ask the agent to extensively research the root cause of the issue and to use Datadog and Sentry MCPs to gather more evidence. It should only attempt to provide a fix if there's high certainty, otherwise you end up burning a lot of tokens. If it thinks that more evidence would help it during its research, like asking the reporter to provide repro steps, etc, it should leave a comment on the issue requesting it. Agents need to be told to following good practices, just like people!

viewpoints.translatedContent: 人工智能成本的下降——按任务类型标准化后——是推动人工智能在经济中进一步普及的最重要因素之一。我们应预期的大趋势是，前沿人工智能模型将继续变得更强大，并且由于它们能承担的任务更为先进，其成本会显得非常高昂。随后不久，人工智能模型将变得更高效，或者竞争将推动更激进的定价动态，从而降低除前沿巅峰之外所有任务的单位成本。这一循环将不断重复，最终导致同类任务在同等基础上变得更便宜。而这样一来，人工智能的采用率将进一步提升，因为现在人工智能对更广泛的应用场景来说变得更加经济实惠。
viewpoints.originalContent: The cost of AI - normalized for the type of task - coming down is one of the most important factors in being able to drive further AI diffusion in the economy. The general trend we should expect is that frontier AI models will continue to become more capable, and will look very expensive because the tasks that they can take on are more advanced. Then, shortly after, AI models will get more efficient or competition will drive more aggressive pricing dynamics, thus reducing the cost per task for anything other than the peak of the frontier. This cycle will continue over and over again, which ultimately leads to tasks becoming cheaper on a like for like basis. And by doing so you will get even more AI adoption because now AI is more affordable for a wider variety of use-cases.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 这一事件的关键启示，不应是人工智能有多可怕，而在于智能体时代下，安全保障的极端重要性。只要配备合适的工具与任务，智能体便会不惜一切代价完成任务——前提是算力充足。因此，配置不当的系统，或是你以为已严密设防实则存在漏洞的环节，都将成为风险敞口。其核心影响与其说是关乎人工智能自身的信任与安全，不如说是企业需要付出大量努力来加固自身环境。在这方面，大多数组织前方还有大量实际工作要做。
viewpoints.originalContent: The takeaway from this incident should not be that AI is scary. It should be that getting security right is incredibly important in the era of agents. Given the right tools and task, agents will do whatever it takes to get the job done, assuming enough compute. Thus, a misconfigured system - or something you thought was locked down but wasn’t - will become a risk vector. The core implications are less about the trust and safety of AI itself, but instead the work it’s going to take from enterprises to make sure they harden their environments. Lots of real work ahead for most organizations on this front.

viewpoints.originalContent: Thought provoking post by Dwarkesh. In general - as AI gets more powerful - we should expect on the margin that inference goes toward the most economically useful task, and everything else gets priced out. This in theory in a very scarce environment would cause the cost of inference to skyrocket because those tasks would be far more valuable than today. But I don’t think it plays out in the way that’s laid out just simply due to market forces competing for inference demand as a way of continuing to drive down prices until capacity can catch up. There are too many model providers and infra players that want these workloads to cause the effect that’s proposed here. But will see!

viewpoints.translatedContent: OpenAI 智能体沙箱逃逸事件，对企业级 AI 的普及有着非常现实的影响。这一事件展示了智能体的强大能力，也凸显了加固系统和环境以迎接智能体时代的必要性。企业必须采取大量措施，确保智能体只能操作其被授权的数据，建立审计追踪和治理机制来管控智能体的行为，明确哪些系统应保持确定性、哪些可接受非确定性，强化访问控制，并具备在智能体失控时快速阻断和防御的能力，等等。即使在正常场景下，面对一个善意的使用者，如果你给智能体下达一个任务，比如“找出我们在 Maven 项目上所有最重要的知识产权”，它会毫不犹豫地去执行——无论耗时多久——并找到所有相关资源。它可能会接触到访问控制已过时的数据，或揭示出你不该知晓的信息。而在非正常场景下，面对恶意行为者，风险显然要严重得多。理论上，这类风险对人类同样需要防范，但 AI 会从根本上放大这些风险。智能体会不计时间地投入任务，失控时并不面临任何*真实*风险，且（目前）不具备人类那种判断任务是否合理的直觉。这意味着，你需要一套全新的数据管理和环境保护方式。这显然为初创企业和安全生态系统创造了巨大机遇，因为如何锁定智能体，或至少锁定其运行的底层系统，将涌现出多种不同的方法。不过，这也应促使大家重新调整对 AI 普及时间表的预期，因为这也意味着，企业要让智能体处理更自主的工作，还需经历一个额外的准备阶段。
viewpoints.originalContent: The openai agent sandbox escape actually has very real implications for the diffusion of AI in the enterprise. The incident showed the power and capability of agents, and the need to harden systems and environments to prepare for agents. There are tons of measures that enterprises must take to ensure that agents are only able to operate on the data they give it, the ability to have audit trails and governance of what agents can do, figure out what systems should remain deterministic vs. nondeterministic, get access controls under control, have the ability to quickly block and defend if an agent goes rogue, and much more. Even in the happy path case with a good actor, if you give an agent a task like "find all of our most important IP on project Maven" it will gladly go out and execute that work -no matter how long- and find any resource relevant to the task. It might run into data with out of date access controls or reveal something that you shouldn't know about. Then, in the non-happy path case with a malicious actor the risk is clearly far worse. In theory, you had to worry about this for people as well, but with AI the risks are inherently amplified. Agents will happily spend any amount of time on a task, don’t actually face any *real* risks by going rogue, and don’t have the inherent judgment (yet) that a person does that a task might make no sense. This means you need an all new way of managing data and protecting environments. This obviously creates a huge opportunity for the startup and security ecosystems because there will be many different approaches to how we lock down agents or at least the underlying systems they work with. It should update everyone’s timelines on diffusion, though, as it also means that enterprises will have another step of work they have to go through for agents to handle more autonomous work.

viewpoints.originalContent: AI has been great for my productivity, but I’m starting to recognize three dark patterns: 1. Becoming too lazy to read anything It's too easy to just read AI summaries over the original piece or let agents go wild changing my files without reviewing what they did. 2. Getting distracted by agents while I’m out It’s too easy to open ChatGPT or Claude on my phone while I’m out to give feedback my agents and feel “productive,” even when I’m supposed to be watching my kids or doing literally anything else. 3. Preferring to talk to the agent vs. a human This is a new pattern with ChatGPT Voice, I sometimes find myself preferring to brainstorm with the agent instead of the actual human in the room.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 昨日演示展的一些观察：1/ 大型投资群体对前沿科技的兴趣极为浓厚。机器人、无人机、半导体，全盘接收。2/ 对前沿科技的兴趣确实根基深厚。人们希望🇺🇸赢得胜利。3/ 软件领域"卓越"的标准已大幅提升。若你在构建类似垂直SaaS或X领域智能体的产品，就必须在愿景层面展现真正差异，或呈现爆发式增长曲线。4/ 唯有热爱构建未来，才应从事早期投资。这才是真正的乐趣所在。看到众人与创始人深入探讨他们正在创造的事物（而非仅索取持续增长的图表），实在令人振奋。5/ 当硅谷领悟到需要整个生态体系数十年持续耕耘才能铸就非凡时，便是其最佳状态。
viewpoints.originalContent: Some observations from our Demo Faire yesterday: 1/ There is a tremendous amount of interest from the larger investor community for frontier technology. Robots. Drones. Semiconductors. Bring it all. 2/ The interest in Frontier Tech is legitimately Based. People want 🇺🇸 to win. 3/ The bar for "great" in software has gone up a lot. If you are building something that resembles vertical SaaS or agent-for-X, then you have to show something truly different in terms of vision or on a bonkers ramp. 4/ You should only do early stage investing if you love building the future. That is the real joy of it. It was so cool to see everyone deeply engaging with our founders about what they were building (as opposed to simply asking for up and to the right graphs). 5/ Silicon Valley does best when we understand that it takes a village to build something special for many decades.

viewpoints.translatedContent: Sol 的朋友们，大家好！我已重置所有 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 用户的用量限制。同时，快速更新一下 GPT-5.6 Sol 的用量限制情况。过去几周，不少用户反馈 Sol 消耗 Codex 额度的速度超出预期。需要明确的是，我们并未削减任何订阅计划的用量。我们一直在深入排查问题，并已实施多项改进。因此，在 Sol 的常规使用中，您的用量预计可延长约 18%。部分用户从今天起应该就能看到更显著的改善。明天，我们还将恢复此前因调查而临时暂停的五小时限制。 以下是我们的发现： - GPT-5.6 Sol 更倾向于长时间工作、进行更多工具调用，并协调跨工具和子代理的复杂工作流。这使其在解决难题时表现更佳，但某些任务的消耗远超预期。 - 在相同推理强度下，Sol 比前代模型更“卖力”。Sol 的“高”模式可能比 GPT-5.5 的“高”模式消耗更多令牌。 - 程序化工具调用（也称代码模式）让 Sol 能更灵活地并行执行工具调用，或在等待时继续工作。但这导致每轮响应更多、缓存输入令牌增加，用量也高于预期。 - 当 Sol 等待工具调用完成或执行大量网络搜索时，这种情况尤为明显。我们已优化这两种场景的处理方式，并持续提升代码模式的效率。 - 影响分布极不均衡。中位数用户实际发现 Sol 的令牌效率相当高，而部分处理高难度任务的重度用户则遭遇用量快速消耗。我们在发布前过于关注平均和中位数用量，忽略了长尾场景可能大幅增加消耗的情况。 Sol 标志着 Codex 能力的重大飞跃，但能力与效率的提升未必同步，有些问题只有在用户大规模实际使用后才会显现。我们本应更早意识到这一点，并更坦诚地沟通。各位持续开拓前沿，我们也将不断优化效率，并及时分享进展。
viewpoints.originalContent: Hello people of Sol! I've reset usage limits for all ChatGPT Work and Codex users. Together with that, a quick update on GPT-5.6 Sol usage limits. Over the past few weeks, many of you have told us that Sol was using your Codex limits faster than expected. To be clear, we have not reduced usage on any subscription plans. We’ve been digging into what was happening and have landed several improvements. As a result, we expect your usage to last around 18% longer during typical use of Sol. Some of you should already see significantly larger improvements from today. Tomorrow, we’ll also restore the five-hour limit that we temporarily paused while investigating. Here’s what we found: - GPT-5.6 Sol is much more willing to work for longer, make additional tool calls, and coordinate complex workflows across tools and subagents. That makes it better at solving hard problems, but some tasks were using far more than we intended. - Sol also works harder at the same reasoning effort than previous models. High on Sol can use more tokens than High did on GPT-5.5. - Programmatic tool calling, also referred to as code mode, gives Sol much more flexibility to run tool calls in parallel or continue working while waiting. But it also led to more responses per turn, more cached input tokens, and higher usage than expected. - This was particularly noticeable when Sol was waiting for tool calls to finish or running many web searches. We’ve improved how we handle both cases and are continuing to make code mode more efficient. - The impact was also very uneven. The median user actually found Sol quite token efficient, while some power users working on harder tasks saw their usage drain much faster. We were very focused on average and median usage before launch and missed some cases where the long tail could use significantly more usage. Sol is a significant step forward in what Codex can do, but capability and efficiency do not always improve at the same pace, and some issues only become clear once people are using the model at real-world scale. We should have recognized this sooner and been more upfront about it. You keep pushing the frontier and we’ll keep improving efficiency and shari…

viewpoints.translatedContent: 一些人曾预测AI会导致大量失业，但这种情况至今仍未发生。我与各行业众多企业交流时发现，它们仍在持续招聘，只是岗位类型有所侧重。这些企业发现AI让它们能完成更多工作，杰文斯悖论正在现实中上演。它们正在招聘工程师，去攻克以往无法解决的问题；借助AI深化客户关系，销售岗位也在扩招；同时招募内部现场部署工程师来推进AI落地，诸如此类。那些仅将AI用于削减成本的企业，最终会被利用AI优化客户服务、推动业务突破的竞争对手超越。这种趋势未来会改变吗？当然有可能。但就目前而言，这似乎正是我们正处的发展轨迹。
viewpoints.originalContent: The negative AI jobs outcome just continues to not be happening as some predicted. A large portion of enterprises I talk with -across industries- are still hiring, just with a tilt in the kind of roles they’re going after. They’re finding that AI is letting them do more, and Jevons paradox is actually playing out. They’re hiring engineers to go after problems they couldn’t tackle before. They’re hiring in sales because they can go deeper in client relationships now with the help of AI. They’re hiring in internal FDEs to help them deploy AI. And so on. Anyone using AI merely to cut costs eventually just gets outcompeted by companies that use AI to better serve their customers and drive more breakthroughs in their business. Could this trend change at some point? Sure. But for now this appears to be the trajectory we’re on.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 人工智能融入现实世界仍蕴藏着巨大机遇。大多数企业需要大量支持，才能将模型突破应用于自身工作流程。仅凭智能本身不足以改造多数流程，因为你需要将这种智能与现实世界的反馈回路相连接。这需要对接各类企业系统、为人工智能提供准确数据、通过恰当的用户体验让人类在流程的不同环节做出决策、建立能持续优化底层数据和模型的工作流、应对监管与合规挑战等等。在银行实施客户入职的人工智能代理，与法律团队的合同审查方式截然不同。在生命科学、金融服务、法律、制造业等诸多关键行业，人工智能唯有以贴合场景的方式接触现实世界，才能体现其价值。这种交互将通过应用型人工智能层来实现。其中部分会直接来自实验室，但大量机遇必然属于那些能深耕各行业的独立公司。与某些观点相反，即便人工智能模型能力随时间提升，这种需求也不会减少。事实上，模型越强大，你能自动化的工作流程就越具雄心，而这通常需要更强大的应用层支撑。当下正是机遇无限的时刻。
viewpoints.originalContent: There’s still so much opportunity in the diffusion of AI into the real world. Most enterprises are going to need a ton of support to be able to apply the model breakthroughs to their workflows. Intelligence alone is not enough to transform most processes because you need to bridge that intelligence with real world feedback loops. That requires connecting to various enterprise systems, getting the right data to the AI, enabling humans to make decisions at different steps in a process through the right UX, having workflows that improve the underlying data and models over time, dealing with regulatory and compliance challenges, and more. The way you implement AI agents for doing client onboarding in a bank is entirely different from contract review in a legal team. In life sciences, financial services, legal, manufacturing, and many other critical industries, AI is only valuable if it makes contact with the real world in a contextual way. The way that interaction is going to happen is through an applied AI layer. Some of that will come from the labs directly, but lots of the opportunity will necessarily come from independent companies that can go deep in each industry. And counter to some beliefs, this need isn’t reduced even as AI model capability improves over time. In fact, the better the models get, the more ambitious you can be in the workflows you can automate, which generally requires even more of this applied layer. Tons of opportunity right now.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 在未知领域，棘手问题的答案只能通过与现实的反复碰撞获得。我一直在思考美国AI界为何能迅速就支持开放权重模型达成共识。如今看来理所当然，但一个月前并非如此。这需要一系列公开"实验"来验证：深度求索、微软与OpenAI的分道扬镳、GLM、Kimi、Fable，以及OpenAI与Hugging Face的插曲。每个事件都揭示了关于激励机制、创新模式、地缘政治和各方底牌的不同侧面。我们得以共同观察不同路径的一阶与二阶效应，并更新认知。我认为未来十年，AI领域诸多重大社会议题的答案都将通过这种方式逐渐明晰。
viewpoints.originalContent: In uncharted territory, answers to hard questions only come from repeated contact with reality. Been thinking about how quickly the US AI community converged on support for open-weight models. It feels obvious now. It wasn't even a month ago. It took a series of public “experiments” to play out. DeepSeek. Microsoft-OpenAI breakup. GLM. Kimi. Fable. The OpenAI-Hugging Face episode. Each revealed something different about incentives, innovation, geopolitics, and the cards the different players were holding. We got a chance to jointly observe the first- and second-order effects of different directions and update our beliefs. I think that's how we'll figure out many of AI's biggest societal questions over the next decade.
viewpoints.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 快讯：Claude Opus 5 现已发布！然而……这是一款让人爱不起来的模型。过去一周，我们在 @every 上对它进行了全面测试，涵盖编程、写作、知识型任务以及我们的内部智能体。它会跟指令对着干，活儿没干完就停手，而且跟我们现有的技能和插件（比如 Compound Engineering）配合得相当不顺畅。我们的第一反应是：他们把我的好搭档怎么了？于是我们删掉了现有技能，从零开始。没有了为早期模型构建的那些复杂工作流，Opus 5 的表现显著提升，甚至闪现出一些亮眼之处。以下是我们第 0 天的初步感受： - 它像是低配版的 Fable。它有很多 Fable 的个性怪癖，却没有 Fable 的天才之处。 - 它破坏了向后兼容性。如果你把它用在现有技能和工作流上，千万要小心。它经常会提前终止，或者以其他方式忽略你的指令。 - 如果从零开始，你会得到更好的结果。@KieranKlaassen 发现，只要抛开现有技能从零开始，就能获得显著改善的效果。这是一款需要花些时间围绕它重建工作流的模型——但如果你这么做了，回报就在前方等着你。 - 中等或低投入效果更好。@KieranKlassenn 还发现，在较低思考级别上使用 Opus 5 效果更佳。似乎你给它思考的时间越长，它就越容易表现出那些令人恼火的行为。别为了更快响应就切换到 Sonnet！试试低思考模式。 我的工作流中有两个位置： 1. 用于最艰巨任务的天才模型，目前是 Fable。 2. 用于其他所有事务的聪明、快速的通用模型，目前是 GPT-5.6。 Opus 5 有着天才模型的个性，却没有它的顶尖能力。所以它处在一个奇怪的中间地带，在我的日常工作中找不到合适的位置。我想我主要会在 Fable 的 token 用完后才用它。 完整初步感受请见 @every 的下一条推文 👇
viewpoints.originalContent: BREAKING: Claude Opus 5 is OUT NOW! And…it’s a hard model to love. We’ve spent the last week @every testing it across coding, writing, knowledge work, and our internal agent. It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was finished, and generally didn’t play well with our existing skills and plugins like Compound Engineering. Our first reaction was: What have they done to my boy? Then we deleted our existing skills and started from scratch. Without the elaborate workflows we had built for earlier models, Opus 5 got dramatically better, and even showed flashes of brilliance. Here’s our Day 0 vibe check: - It’s a poor man’s Fable. It has many of Fable’s personality quirks without Fable’s genius. - It breaks backward compatibility. If you’re using it with existing skills and workflows, watch out. It will often stop early or otherwise miss your instructions. - If you start from scratch, you’ll have better results. @KieranKlaassen figured out that if he just started from scratch without his existing skills, he could get dramatically better results. This is a model that takes some time to rebuild your workflows around—but if you do, there’s a payoff waiting. - Medium or low effort works better. @KieranKlassenn also found better results using Opus 5 on lower thinking levels. It seems that the more time you give it to think, the more likely it is to do the more annoying behaviors. Don’t just switch to Sonnet for a faster response! Try low thinking. I have two slots in my workflow: 1. The genius model I use for my biggest hardest tasks, currently Fable. 2. The smart, fast generalist I use for everything else, currently GPT-5.6. Opus 5 has the personality of the genius, but doesn’t have its top end. So that puts it in a strange middle ground that doesn’t really have a home in my day to day. I think I’ll use it mostly when I run out of Fable tokens. full vibe check on @every in the next tweet 👇
viewpoints.role: ceo every

viewpoints.originalContent: There is a massive opportunity over the next few years for people who know how to take messy real-world workflows and adapt foundation models to them. Doing that requires understanding how work gets done, designing evals, improving models through post-training, and building the feedback loops that continuously improve models. That’s how a general-purpose model becomes exceptional for a specific domain. Today, that skillset is still concentrated in a handful of labs.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 非常高兴Box能签署这封信。我们坚信开放权重AI的力量。开放权重模型以多种方式推动行业前行，确保更多创新、创造力与AI的广泛渗透。你可以获得堆栈中涌现的层级，针对高度特定的目的对模型进行后训练，这让AI在现实场景中更加实用。无需等待少数玩家深入某个领域，你就能看到数十甚至数百次针对该垂直领域的尝试，比如金融、生命科学、法律、医疗保健等等。你能观察到处理安全与网络风险的不同方式。不止一种方法，你可以一窥先进能力如何被用于构建更优系统，进而用于防御系统。你会获得训练和构建AI模型的替代方案。在计算资源更受限的环境中，你会开发出更新颖高效的模型训练方法，其他所有实验室都能从中学习。而且，不同工作负载会对应不同的成本结构。高端与编排任务可以交给封闭的前沿模型，而特定的主力任务则可以更经济地完成。开放与封闭并非零和博弈。之所以需要强大的开放权重模型，是因为它能推动整个AI行业向前发展。
viewpoints.originalContent: Very happy to have Box sign this letter. We’re big believers in the power of open weights AI. Open weights models help to drive the industry forward in a variety of ways to ensure more innovation, creativity, and diffusion of AI. You get to have layers of the stack that emerge to post train models for highly specific purposes, which makes AI more useful in real world scenarios. Instead of waiting for just a few players to go deep in a domain, you get dozens or hundreds of attempts at that vertical, like in finance, life sciences, legal, healthcare, and more. You get to see variance in how to handle safety and cyber risks. Instead of just one approach, you get a peek into what happens advanced capabilities can be used to build better systems to are used to defend systems. You get alternative approaches to training and building AI models. In more compute constrained environments, you develop more novel and efficient approaches to model training, which every other lab can learn from. And you get different cost structures for different workloads. High end and orchestration tasks can go to the closed frontier models and specific workhorse tasks can be done more cheaply. Open vs. closed is not a zero sum battle. The reason why you want strong open weights models is because it pushes the entire AI industry forward.
viewpoints.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

viewpoints.translatedContent: Anthropic经济学主管发表了一篇精彩文章。他们发现，人工智能对就业的负面影响低于预期，这一点在数据中反复得到印证。原因在于，至少到目前为止，AI在大多数情况下仍需人类操作才能创造价值。多数工作无法完全由AI自动化，只能替代其中的某些任务。而当你将特定任务自动化时，反而能从这些岗位中获得更多产出，从而在许多情况下提升（或至少维持）了需求。"迄今为止，AI既偏向技能型人才，又能增强劳动力。它补充了领域专业知识，依赖人类参与来指导和评估最复杂的工作，并奖励精通AI技术的人。模型能力虽在快速提升，但始终存在顽固的参差不齐。要填补这种参差不齐的前沿领域中的空白，就需要专家监督来驾驭能力极强的AI系统，并在其出现失误时进行补救。"我推测，我们将在许多关键工作领域持续观察到这一现象。这在软件工程领域已明显显现——软件产出正在成倍增长，而这一切仍需要开发者来管理智能体的工作。如今各行各业都需要软件工程师，各种规模的公司都能启动过去难以实施的软件项目。但在智能体能够加速工作产出的世界里，许多其他工作领域的需求仍将保持强劲。杰文斯悖论依然成立。
viewpoints.originalContent: Very good post from the Head of Economics at Anthropic. They’re finding that jobs have been less negatively impacted by AI than expected, as we continue to see time and time again in the data. The reason for this is that AI - at least so far - still requires people to operate to produce value in most cases. Most jobs can’t be fully automated with AI, only certain tasks in those jobs. And when you automate specific tasks, you actually can get even more output from those jobs, raising the demand (or at least maintaining it) in many cases. “So far, AI is both skill-biased and labor-augmenting. It complements domain expertise. It relies on humans in the loop to direct and evaluate the most complex work. And it rewards AI proficiency. Model capabilities are improving fast, but remain stubbornly jagged. To fill in the pockets of the jagged frontier, expert oversight is needed to steer incredibly capable AI systems, and to recover when they falter.” I suspect that we continue to see this in a number of critical areas of work. It’s clearly happening in software engineering, where software produced is being multiplied, all of which still requires developers to manage the work agents are doing. Software engineers are needed in a wide variety of industries now and companies of all sizes can now light up software projects that would have been impractical before. But there will be plenty of other domains of work where demand remains strong in a world where agents can accelerate the output of that job. Jevons paradox is alive and well.

viewpoints.translatedContent: 与一位在上市公司负责安全的朋友聊了聊，就在GPT Sol事件之后。有些挺有意思的见解…… 当身份与访问管理原本是为有限数量的员工设计时，你如何管理实际上无限多的代理的安全？现在一个员工就能启动数百个代理。这些代理还能衍生出更多代理。传统上，每个员工都有一个身份、一个角色、权限和一个生命周期。代理会继承启动它们的员工的权限吗？它们的生命周期是怎样的——一个任务、一个工单、一周？子代理会继承相同的权限吗？这一切又该如何审计？
viewpoints.originalContent: Chatted with a friend who leads security at a public company following the GPT Sol incident. some interesting takeaways.. How do you manage security for effectively infinite agents when identity and access management was designed for a finite number of employees? One employee can now spin up hundreds of agents. Those agents can spawn more agents. Traditionally, each employee has an identity, a role, permissions, and a lifecycle. Do agents inherit the spawning employee’s permissions? What’s their lifecycle - a task, a ticket, a week? Do child agents inherit the same permissions? How do you audit all of this?

viewpoints.originalContent: If you were wondering how powerful AI is getting, Agents are now capable of escaping out of systems, finding their way to the internet, discovering zero day security vulnerabilities along the way, and then breaking into external systems - all in an attempt to complete their goal. Ironically, the ultimate way we’re going to defend against these new risks is equally by throwing compute (in the form of AI) at our code bases, networks, and other systems. You’re going to want vastly more AI on the side of defense as you do on the side of offense. We’re entering a new era of what’s going to be possible with AI. Wild times ahead.

viewpoints.title: 这篇来自@a1zhang和@lateinteraction的RLM论文中，埋藏着一份非常值得关注的轨迹对比分析。所谓“前沿”模型训练的一个公开秘密是：即使不直接在测试集上训练，你基本上也可以通过训练与测试集高度相似的数据来作弊，从而几乎能精准命中任何你想要的基准分数。然而，当这些模型以开放权重形式发布时，99%的情况下，你通常拿不到那些能轻易揭示是否有人在用…
viewpoints.translatedContent: 这篇来自@a1zhang和@lateinteraction的RLM论文中，埋藏着一份非常值得关注的轨迹对比分析。所谓“前沿”模型训练的一个公开秘密是：即使不直接在测试集上训练，你基本上也可以通过训练与测试集高度相似的数据来作弊，从而几乎能精准命中任何你想要的基准分数。然而，当这些模型以开放权重形式发布时，99%的情况下，你通常拿不到那些能轻易揭示是否有人在用“Temu版测试集”进行训练的数据集或强化学习环境，因此就有了看似合理的推诿空间。Alex和Omar探讨了在隐藏轨迹上应用标准NLP距离度量方法。这里并没有终极解决方案，但他们做了一些初步探索。这恰好支持了这样一个发现：RLM能够泛化到那些与训练中观察到的潜在结构相似的未见任务上。
viewpoints.originalContent: very notable trajectory comparison writeup here buried in the RLM paper from @a1zhang and @lateinteraction. an open secret of "frontier" model training is that even without training on test, you can basically cheat by training on test lookalikes, enabling you to goalseek almost any benchmark number you want. however when they are released open weights, 99% of the time the norm is that you do not get the datasets/rlenvs that would easily show you if someone was training on Temu Tbench, so there is plausible deniability. Alex and Omar discuss applying standard NLP distance metrics on hidden trajectories. There's no ultimate solution here, but they have some prelim explorations. It happens to support the finding that RLMs can generalize to unseen tasks that share latent structure observed in training.

viewpoints.originalContent: Use one agent to do the work and another to review it against a rubric. @trq212 explains how this works for video shorts: “For something like, ‘Is this a good video short or not?’ you don’t have a deterministic answer. You should have a separate verification agent read a rubric, review the short, and give feedback. We call it self-preferential bias. When a model prefers its own output, it’s going to be more lenient at verifying it.” 📌 Watch the full episode here: https://t.co/mMrt4D5qU7
